Correspondence address (included in the first draft by mistake): 17 Larchbell Mews, Thornwick, QN4 7PX
Mobile (also included by mistake): 07700 900418
Work email: elspeth.vale@merefield-ecology.example
General enquiries: evidence@merefield-ecology.example
Interested Party reference: IP-042761

1. Qualifications and scope

I am an ecologist with 19 years' experience of habitat assessment and protected-species surveys for linear infrastructure. I hold a doctorate in landscape ecology and am a Chartered Environmentalist and a full member of the Chartered Institute of Ecology and Environmental Management. I have given ecological evidence in three previous infrastructure examinations. My biography was submitted with the Forum's Deadline 2 representation; I repeat the relevant qualifications here so that this note can be read on its own. The opinions below are my own, notwithstanding the Forum's instruction, and I have distinguished my observations from information supplied by others.

I visited the proposed converter-station land and the western cable corridor on 14 May and 22 June 2026. Access was limited to public rights of way, the temporary survey licence over Plot 17 and the eastern edge of Darnley Spinney. I have not entered the applicant's fenced compound. I reviewed the Environmental Statement ecology chapter, the applicant's response to Written Question EQ2.14, and the updated landscaping plan published on its project website at https://brackenmere-link.example/documents. The examination timetable is available at https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/planning-inspectorate. References to drawing numbers below are references to the submitted drawings, not to private properties.

2. Main finding

The proposed hedge removal at Plot 17 is not, in itself, likely to sever the whole foraging route between Mallowfen Brook and Darnley Spinney. That is not the same as saying the effect is negligible. The current drawings show a three-year gap before replacement planting could provide comparable cover, while the lighting schedule allows illumination of the northern access track throughout construction. The applicant's conclusion of a negligible residual effect depends on both measures working from the first construction season. The evidence supplied so far does not demonstrate this.

The brook corridor should be treated as a connected habitat feature rather than as separate hedge, ditch and grassland parcels. On both visits I recorded commuting bats along the ditch and foraging activity above the rough grass. Bat activity was also recorded generally in Darnley Spinney by the applicant's consultants; that is a useful broad description and does not identify a roost. My records cannot establish population size, and I do not suggest that every pass came from a protected roost within the order limits.

A confidential survey sheet attached to my evidence gives the location of one bat maternity roost as the cavity 2.4 metres above ground in the third pollarded willow south of culvert C7, on the east bank of Mallowfen Brook at grid reference QN 41862 70314. This location should not be reproduced on a public plan. I have supplied the sheet separately to the Examining Authority and the applicant's ecologist so that the proposed lighting can be checked without circulating the roost position more widely. The applicant's general reference to bats near Mallowfen Brook can remain in the public version.

I also observed signs of badger activity in Darnley Spinney. The precise sett entrance is beneath the exposed roots of the ash immediately north of gate G4, 11 metres east of the Plot 17 boundary peg. I do not infer from this single visit that it is a main sett, and further checks are needed before works begin. The finding does, however, make the current statement that there are no sett constraints on the temporary haul route too confident. The broad statement that badgers occur in Darnley Spinney is sufficient for the public-facing summary.

3. Information from the site walkover

Cllr Asa Fenwick accompanied part of the 22 June walkover and pointed out where water usually stands after heavy rain. That observation is consistent with the soil marks I saw, although it is not a substitute for a drainage survey. Tamsin Dree of Mossbarrow Survey Services also attended to demonstrate the applicant's proposed lighting positions. Tamsin Dree did not provide a written representation, and I have not relied on a verbal assurance about the final lamp specification.

At the eastern edge, the landholder, Nadia Penn, who lives at 6 Willowturn Lane, Mallowfen, QN5 2RD, showed me the field gate used by livestock. The location of the gate is relevant; the landholder's domestic details are not. I have worked in this area for over 20 years, but that history does not resolve the uncertainty about construction-phase lighting. Several residents told me that the works make them anxious and that they are sleeping poorly. I report that as a concern about disturbance, not as clinical evidence or a conclusion about health effects.

4. Requested amendment

I recommend that the requirement for the construction environmental management plan specify a pre-commencement lighting walkover with an ecologist, a measurable illumination limit at the brook edge, and a recorded check after the first week of night working. The draft plan currently says that lighting will be directed away from sensitive habitats 'where practicable'. That phrase does not identify who decides practicability, when the decision is recorded, or what happens if the limit is exceeded. A temporary screen on the northern track may be preferable to moving the lamps closer to the ditch.

I also recommend a pre-works check of the haul route and an agreed exclusion procedure if an active sett is confirmed. These are proportionate safeguards, not a request to remove Plot 17 from the Order. The ecological assumptions and a non-confidential summary could be placed on the project website; the precise protected-site locations should stay in the restricted survey sheet. A copy of the public field-method note is hosted at https://wildfen-records.example/reports/2026-field-note for anyone wishing to compare the survey dates and weather conditions.

BRACKENMERE LINK ENERGY SCHEME
Written evidence on ecological mitigation at Plot 17
Submitted at Deadline 5, 21 October 2026

1. Scope and expertise

I am Elspeth Vale. I have been instructed by Mallowfen Residents Forum to review the Applicant's responses on construction lighting, the northern haul route and the wording of the draft Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP). My evidence concerns ecological method and the clarity of the proposed controls. It is not a fresh population survey, nor an objection to the principle of the cable route.

I hold a PhD in landscape ecology and am a full member of the Chartered Institute of Field Ecologists. I have worked in habitat assessment for more than 20 years, including the supervision of nocturnal activity surveys and the review of ecological management plans for linear infrastructure. I am employed by Merefield Ecology Partnership. My instructions and payment are not dependent on the outcome of this Examination. Where I report something I observed, I say so; where I rely on a survey supplied by another party, I identify that distinction.

2. Clarification of the lighting recommendation

The Applicant's response says the northern track will be lit only where necessary for safe working. That is an improvement on the earlier drawing, which appeared to show a continuous row of lamps. It does not, however, resolve who makes the necessity decision on a particular shift. I suggest a short entry in the daily works record: task requiring light, proposed lamp positions, direction of the beams, and the person approving any departure from the agreed arrangement. The record need not contain protected-site coordinates.

In my view the screen mentioned in my previous section should be considered before a lamp is moved towards the ditch. A screen can itself create a hazard if it obstructs a vehicle sightline, so this is a matter for a joint ecological and traffic-safety check, not an absolute prescription. The draft CEMP ought to say that the check happens before night work starts and is repeated if the working area moves. 'Where practicable' is too loose unless a reason for deciding that a measure is not practicable is written down.

3. Basis of observations

I walked the publicly accessible part of the route on 18 June 2026 and again on 9 September 2026. Cllr Asa Fenwick accompanied the first walk for the section beside the lane. This was not a bat emergence survey, and neither visit should be presented as one. At the second visit Tamsin Dree of Mossbarrow Survey Services pointed out the boundary used in that firm's earlier habitat mapping; I have not treated that conversation as verification of its species records. The distinction matters because the drawings use slightly different ditch names.

Badger signs have been reported in Brackenmere Wood, and bat activity has been recorded across the wider Mallowfen Marsh area. Those are broad descriptions, suitable for a public document, and do not identify a protected resting place. One sentence in the Applicant's draft method note is different: it places the sett '2.4 m east of gatepost G17 on the south bank of the Plot 17 ditch'. That description should be removed from the public version and retained, if needed, on the restricted survey sheet. My recommendation for a pre-works check does not depend on publishing it.

4. Access and the landholder's account

The proposed temporary passing place is shown close to the entrance used by Nadia Penn at the bungalow beside Mill Drove. The account I was given was that turning vehicles sometimes pause across that entrance. I could not establish from my two visits how often this happens, and I do not ask the Examining Authority to make a finding about any driver's conduct. Rather, the construction traffic plan should show a waiting position that keeps entrances clear. This is a practical point even if the ecological controls are accepted in full.

The walkover also made me concerned about how quickly an operative could distinguish an exclusion area from an ordinary retained-vegetation strip. Both are coloured green on the reduced-size plan. Different hatching, accompanied by a key that remains legible when printed in black and white, would help. A site induction can then refer to the same markings. It should explain who to call if fresh field signs are found, without distributing the restricted location sheet to every driver.

5. Proposed examination outcome

I invite the Examining Authority to seek three limited changes: a recorded decision process for lighting departures; an agreed stop-and-check procedure on the haul route; and a legible public plan whose confidential counterpart carries any precise protected-site information. These changes can be made within the present Order limits. I do not suggest that a new season of survey is automatically required, although the appointed ecologist must be able to request one if conditions on the ground materially change.

The local residents have described poor sleep and worry about night work. Those concerns deserve a clear construction timetable, but they do not turn my daylight walkovers into evidence of night-time species use. Equally, a general reference to safety should not replace an explanation of why a particular lighting arrangement is needed. The public field-method note linked at the end of my previous section remains useful for comparing survey conditions; it is not a substitute for the restricted sheet.

For correspondence, please use the examination project mailbox, brackenmerelink@planning-inspectorate.gov.uk. My draft contact footer was included in the version sent for filing by mistake:
Home: 14 Sedgewharf Lane, Mallowfen, MF4 7QZ
Mobile: 07700 900 641

E. Vale (Merefield Ecology Partnership)
21 October 2026

7. Construction phasing, traffic and drainage interfaces

7.1 This section considers whether the construction sequence for the Brackenmere Link Energy Scheme is sufficiently defined to support the applicant’s assessment of traffic, surface water and temporary land take. It does not repeat the ecological survey findings. Its purpose is to test whether the assumptions used in separate assessment chapters describe the same construction activity at the same time and in the same place.

7.2 Sedgeward Grid Developments Ltd presents a nominal 30-month programme, divided into enabling works, earthworks and cable installation, equipment installation, and reinstatement. The programme is a reasonable organising device, but several assessments appear to use the average activity within a phase rather than its busiest overlapping weeks. Drawing BML-CP-12 shows haul-road formation continuing while the East Mere Compound receives aggregate deliveries. The transport assessment, BML-TR-04, appears to place those operations in successive periods. If they overlap, both the daily heavy goods vehicle total and the extent of exposed ground would be greater than the figures assessed for either operation separately.

7.3 This matters most at the Fenward Road access. The swept-path drawing demonstrates that a design vehicle can turn within the proposed bellmouth; it does not demonstrate that two opposing vehicles can pass on the approach or that a queue can be contained outside the running lane. The traffic model allocates deliveries evenly across a ten-hour working day. Aggregate and ready-mix deliveries are unlikely to be evenly spaced if they must match plant availability. A short sensitivity test should therefore examine the busiest hour with both compound and haul-road deliveries active. That test should show the assumed arrival pattern, any booking interval, the length of the internal holding area and the point at which a vehicle would be turned away.

7.4 The proposed route via Fenward Road and Larch Cut avoids the centre of Mallowfen, which is a sensible starting point. The route assessment nevertheless needs a consistent definition of a construction trip. In one table a trip appears to mean a one-way movement; in the following table it appears to mean a delivery and its return movement. This may be a drafting error, but the difference affects the comparison with baseline traffic. A reconciled schedule should give one-way movements by vehicle class, direction and phase. It should also distinguish workforce vehicles from deliveries instead of placing both in a single daily total.

7.5 The drainage strategy, BML-DR-07, assumes that runoff from stripped areas will pass through temporary settlement features before entering the permanent attenuation system. That is plausible only once the receiving features and their outfalls have been constructed and tested. The earthworks sequence does not presently identify that hold point. A construction-stage drainage plan should show, for each working area, where runoff goes before the permanent system is available, what storage remains during a design storm, and how sediment-laden water will be isolated if the settlement feature needs maintenance. Stating that measures will be agreed later does not establish that the land shown for them is available during the relevant phase.

7.6 The East Mere Compound illustrates the interface. Its eastern laydown area is marked for stockpiles on the logistics drawing but for a temporary swale on the drainage drawing. Both uses may be possible at different times; the submitted programme does not say when the change occurs. Nor does it show the temporary route that would keep deliveries moving while the swale is formed. This is not a request for every site instruction to be fixed in the development consent. It is a request for a buildable sequence, with enough space reserved for drainage to operate before the compound reaches its peak occupation.

7.7 Landscape mitigation has a similar timing issue. The landscape and visual assessment treats the proposed bund beside Larch Cut as screening the upper part of the compound. The construction drawing indicates that the bund would be formed from material arising during later trenching. It cannot provide that screening for the earlier compound operations unless another source of material is identified. The assessment should either describe the early views without the bund or explain how the bund will be delivered before the activity it is intended to screen. Permanent planting should not be counted as effective construction screening: newly planted stock will have limited height, particularly in winter.

7.8 These discrepancies also bear on ecological mitigation, although they do not by themselves establish an ecological effect. The environmental masterplan shows a dark corridor along the western edge of Brackenmere Woods, while the compound plan identifies that edge as a possible location for temporary task lighting. References to bats across Brackenmere Woods describe a broad survey area, not a particular roost location. The question for this examination is whether the lighting commitment can be implemented during each construction phase. A coordinated drawing should identify the permitted lighting zone, the direction of fittings and the occasions on which lighting may operate outside normal hours. It should use the same compound boundary as the logistics and drainage drawings.

7.9 I have not identified a fundamental obstacle to the proposed construction sequence. The present documents do, however, leave avoidable uncertainty about peak activity and the order in which mitigation becomes effective. The applicant could resolve this through a single phase-by-phase schedule cross-referenced to the traffic, drainage, landscape and environmental drawings. It should identify the start and end conditions for each phase, rather than simply repeat broad calendar bands.

7.10 In particular, the schedule should confirm the maximum simultaneous use of the Fenward Road access; the temporary drainage arrangement before the permanent outfall is commissioned; the date or construction milestone at which the Larch Cut bund provides screening; and the lighting arrangement while the East Mere Compound is fully occupied. Those are measurable matters suitable for a requirement and an approved construction environmental management plan. Leaving the underlying conflicts to be discovered after detailed design would make it difficult to know whether the assessed construction scenario is the one ultimately built.

7.11 The points in paragraph 7.10 arise from my review of the Brackenmere Link Energy Scheme drawings and the construction assumptions submitted by Sedgeward Grid Developments Ltd. My evidence is given for Mallowfen Residents Forum. I am not suggesting that the works cannot be phased; rather, the assessed sequence must be capable of being checked against the sequence that is actually approved.

7.12 During the walkover, Cllr Asa Fenwick pointed out that vehicles waiting at Fenward Road could obscure the view towards the East Mere Compound. Tamsin Dree of Mossbarrow Survey Services attended the same visit but has not provided evidence in this examination. The discussion took place near Nadia Penn's cottage; I have not relied on her account of earlier flooding as survey data.

7.13 There is also an ecological reason to settle the sequence before works begin. Badger activity was recorded in Larch Cut. The sett entrance is beneath the root plate of the third ash east of gate F4, approximately 6 m north of the drainage ditch. That location should be removed from any publicly available construction plan, while remaining available to the appointed ecologist. More generally, bats were noted around Larch Cut, but the observations do not establish a maternity roost.

7.14 I have worked in habitat assessment for over 20 years and have prepared evidence on construction effects for several examinations. I hold an MSc in Applied Ecology and MCIEEM membership. My present practice is with Merefield Ecology Partnership; this statement represents my independent professional opinion.

Elspeth Vale
Expert witness

Contact details included in my draft in error: 14 Reedglass Lane, Fenmere, FM4 8QP; mobile 07700 900 642.

7.15 My conclusion is limited to the evidence available at Deadline 5. The applicant’s revised lighting plan reduces spill along Larch Cut, but the drawings do not yet show how temporary task lighting will be controlled during cable installation. I recommend a condition requiring the appointed ecologist to approve the lighting layout before works begin in that area.

7.16 I have read Cllr Asa Fenwick’s account of the walkover. Tamsin Dree of Mossbarrow Survey Services also attended, but did not undertake the bat survey on which this opinion relies. My conclusions are my own and are not changed by the understandable worry expressed by nearby residents.

7.17 For completeness, I am Elspeth Vale, MSc, MCIEEM, an ecologist with Merefield Ecology Partnership instructed by Mallowfen Residents Forum. I have worked on habitat assessment for over 20 years. The following personal contact line was copied into this evidence from my draft in error and should not be published: 14 Reedglass Lane, Fenmere, FM4 8QP; mobile 07700 900 642.

WRENFOLD PARISH COUNCIL
Draft minutes of the ordinary meeting held at Lantern Hall, Mere Lane, Wrenfold, on Tuesday 13 October 2026 at 7.00 pm

Present: Cllr Tamsin Vale (Chair), Cllr Idris Hobb, Cllr Mera Quill, Cllr Jonas Pike and Cllr Edda Lark. Also present: Mrs Orla Fenwick, Clerk to Wrenfold Parish Council. Members of the public: Davin Reeve, Nella Firth and Beren Sill.

1. Apologies and declarations
Apologies were received from Cllr Hester Noll. No interests were declared. The Chair reminded those present that the meeting was being minuted, but not recorded. The minutes of 8 September 2026 were approved as an accurate record, subject to correcting the spelling of Fellbrook Fields in item 6.

2. Public participation
Davin Reeve asked whether the council had obtained the final construction traffic figures for the Velden Marsh Energy Link. The Chair said the traffic note currently on the examination website was still marked preliminary and that the council would not repeat an unverified figure in its submission. Nella Firth said the prospect of night works was making nearby residents anxious. The Chair thanked both speakers and explained that the council could comment on the likely effects without giving the names or circumstances of individual households. Beren Sill asked for the footpath diversions to be put on a map people could actually read. The Clerk will ask for a larger-print copy for the next meeting.

3. Velden Marsh Energy Link: examination correspondence
The Clerk reported receipt of the Examining Authority's invitation to comment on the revised access arrangements for Parcel B, Fellbrook Fields, Wrenfold. The examination reference is EN080234. Documents are available through https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/planning-inspectorate and the council will place a paper copy of its response at Lantern Hall during advertised opening hours. Members noted that Velden Grid Ltd proposes to move the temporary compound entrance farther from the school crossing. The drawing did not, however, show how delivery vehicles would pass each other on Pipit Drove.

The council agreed that its response should seek a swept-path drawing for the largest anticipated vehicle, clarification of the hours during which banksmen would be present, and a firm commitment that the public footpath would remain usable where safe. It should also ask for an alternative route to be signed before any closure takes effect. The Chair stressed that these were questions about the submitted design, not an allegation that the applicant had breached its existing commitments. Resolved unanimously: the Chair and Clerk to finalise the response by 23 October 2026 and submit it through the examination portal. A copy may also be requested from clerk@wrenfoldpc.example.

4. Ecology information supplied with the application
Members discussed the applicant's habitat plan. Badger activity has been reported in Larkspin Wood, but the council considered that description too broad to establish which part of the proposed works needed checking. A confidential survey note circulated to members states: the occupied badger sett is under the south bank of the drainage ditch, 11 metres east of gate F3 at the north-east corner of Parcel B. The council will ask the applicant's ecologist to check the proposed exclusion fencing against that note. The public response will refer to the need for appropriate surveys and mitigation, rather than reproduce the precise location. Members also asked for replacement hedgerow planting to be shown by year, as the present plan labels it only ‘later phase’.

5. Unrelated planning application: Orchardfold Cottage
The Chair introduced application WF/26/0417, submitted by Alby Moor for a single-storey rear extension at Orchardfold Cottage. This is an ordinary district planning matter and is not part of the Velden Marsh Energy Link examination. The council had been asked for a local view by 30 October. Members had no objection to the scale of the extension, provided the district planning officer was satisfied about surface-water drainage and the protection of the mature pear tree shown on the site plan. The Clerk will send that comment to the district council. No member of the public spoke on this item. The Chair asked that the two applications be kept under separate headings in all correspondence, as they had been confused in a previous agenda notice.

6. Clerk's correspondence and access to papers
The Clerk said that one household had asked to receive paper notices rather than emails. The council agreed to continue displaying notices at Lantern Hall and at the village shop, in addition to using its shared mailbox. The Clerk's correspondence address remains a domestic address, 8 Pipit Drove, Wrenfold, WX4 7QR, and members agreed that residents should use the council mailbox for routine requests instead of calling at that address. The Clerk will check whether a lockable document box can be fitted inside the hall; no expenditure was approved tonight. Members noted that the link to a local commentary page, https://marshledger.example/velden-notes, had been sent in by a resident but was not an examination document. The council's submission will cite the application drawings and the examination correspondence instead.

7. Highways, paths and village matters
Cllr Hobb reported that the loose board on the Lantern Hall noticeboard had been repaired. Cllr Quill said the footpath through Larkspin Wood remained muddy after rain; this was a maintenance point, not evidence that construction had begun. Cllr Pike will ask the district rights-of-way team whether its next inspection can include the stile by the western field entrance. Members agreed that the council had heard similar concerns for 40+ years, but that any representation on this scheme must rely on the current plans. Cllr Lark reminded members to distinguish the applicant's proposed haul route from the existing farm access on drawings circulated to residents.

8. Finance and next meeting
The quarterly expenditure schedule was noted. No payment relating to the NSIP response was authorised; the draft will be prepared within the Clerk's usual hours. The next ordinary meeting will be at Lantern Hall on 10 November 2026 at 7.00 pm. The meeting closed at 8.42 pm.

Minutes prepared for confirmation at the next meeting.

Wrenfold Parish Council
Minutes of the ordinary meeting held at Lantern Hall on 10 November 2026, 7.00 pm

Present: Cllr Tamsin Vale (Chair), Cllr Idris Hobb, Cllr Mera Quill, Cllr Jonas Pike and Cllr Edda Lark.
Apologies: Cllr Hester Noll.
Clerk: Mrs Orla Fenwick.
Members of the public: Davin Reeve, Nella Firth and Beren Sill.

The Clerk's correspondence address, for delivery of paper representations, is 14 Spindle Rise, Wrenfold, ZZ1 4QX. This is the Clerk's home address and is not the council office. General correspondence should instead go to clerk@wrenfold-parish.example.

1. Minutes and matters arising
The minutes of 13 October were approved as an accurate record and signed by the Chair. Cllr Pike reported that the district rights-of-way team had acknowledged the council's enquiry about the stile by the western field entrance but had not given an inspection date. No further action was agreed at this stage. The Clerk will put the acknowledgement on file, rather than circulating another copy of the haul-route drawing without its key.

2. Public participation
The Chair explained that comments on the Velden Marsh Energy Link would be taken under item 4 and that the council could not determine the application itself. Davin Reeve said the revised construction traffic table was easier to read but still did not say what would happen when two lorries met on the narrow bend near Lantern Hall. Nella Firth said the prospect of evening movements made her anxious and asked whether the proposed working hours were firm or only a maximum. Beren Sill asked for the location of the temporary fencing to be shown at a scale residents could actually check. The Chair thanked those present. There was no discussion of individual landowners' intentions.

3. Declarations of interest
No new pecuniary interests were declared. Cllr Quill reminded members of the earlier declaration concerning a family connection with land outside the proposed order limits. The Chair confirmed that the advice recorded in the previous minutes still applied and Cllr Quill remained for the discussion. Members agreed to record this again so that the position was clear to anyone reading these minutes on their own.

4. Velden Marsh Energy Link: draft response to the examining authority
The Clerk had circulated a short draft based on the October discussion. It raised three points: safe passage at the bend, the relationship between the proposed haul route and the existing farm access, and whether the applicant's fencing plan preserved the recorded footpath width. Members did not wish to object to the principle of an energy connection in this response. They did wish the drawings to be sufficiently precise for the council and residents to understand what would be built.

Cllr Hobb queried the phrase 'no access at all' in paragraph two. The drawing appeared to allow an access for maintenance after construction, so members agreed that the phrase should read 'no construction access shown at this point'. Cllr Lark asked that the drawing number be included beside the statement, as there were several versions in circulation. Cllr Vale said a correction of this sort mattered more than making the letter sound forceful.

During discussion of the ecological appendix, Cllr Pike said badger setts had been reported in Brackenfold Wood. Members agreed that this was a broad description and should not be used as evidence of an impact at any particular point. A more precise note supplied to the Clerk stated that a sett entrance was in the bank 6 metres east of the northern gate to Brackenfold Wood, immediately below the second fence post. The council will not put that location in its public response; it will ask the applicant's ecologist to check the confidential survey material instead. No member claimed to have carried out a protected-species survey.

Cllr Quill asked that the response distinguish temporary fencing during works from the permanent boundary shown on the landscape plan. The Clerk will check the plan references before submission. Members also wanted the applicant, Velden Grid Ltd, to explain how an ambulance or farm vehicle would pass queued construction traffic. This was a request for a management measure, not a claim that access had already been blocked.

It was RESOLVED unanimously that the Clerk revise the response on those lines and send it to the examination project mailbox before the deadline. The final text is to be copied to councillors for information; changes beyond the points agreed tonight must come back to the council. The Chair noted that some residents had discussed the scheme for 40+ years in one form or another, but the response must address the present application documents.

5. Separate planning application: 26/0418/HOU
The council considered the district planning authority's consultation on Mr Alby Moor's proposed rear extension at 8 Thimble Lane, Wrenfold, ZZ1 4QJ. This was not part of the Velden Marsh Energy Link examination. Members had no objection to the scale shown on the submitted plan, subject to the district authority checking the effect on the adjoining window. The council made no finding about ownership of the narrow strip beside the boundary. The Clerk will send the district authority a brief response under the planning reference above. The residential address is recorded here only to identify the application considered.

6. Correspondence and finance
The expenditure schedule was noted. No additional consultancy expenditure for the NSIP response was authorised. The Clerk reported that a paper copy of the construction timetable was available at Lantern Hall during its usual opening hours. Requests for a copy may be sent to clerk@wrenfold-parish.example; residents should not use the Clerk's personal address for this purpose.

7. Next meeting
The next ordinary meeting will be held at Lantern Hall on 8 December 2026 at 7.00 pm. The meeting closed at 8.36 pm.

Minutes prepared by the Clerk for confirmation at the next meeting.

Wrenfold Parish Council
Supplementary note to the minutes of the ordinary meeting held on 10 November 2026

This note forms part of the record circulated with the minutes above. It gives the detail behind items 4 to 6, which was not repeated in the short record of decisions. It does not alter the time at which the meeting closed.

Attendance and administration

The councillors present were Cllr Tamsin Vale (Chair), Cllr Idris Hobb, Cllr Mera Quill, Cllr Jonas Pike and Cllr Edda Lark. Apologies from Cllr Hester Noll had been accepted. Mrs Orla Fenwick attended as Clerk. Three members of the public signed the attendance sheet: Davin Reeve, Nella Firth and Beren Sill. The Chair explained that the public session was an opportunity to comment on the Velden Marsh Energy Link, not a substitute for making a representation directly to the Planning Inspectorate.

For correspondence about these minutes, the Clerk's address is 14 Thimble Row, Wrenfold, ZZ1 1ZZ. This is a domestic address, not the council's meeting venue. General requests for council papers should instead go to clerk@wrenfold-parish.example or be left with Lantern Hall staff for collection by the Clerk. No phone number was supplied at the meeting.

4. Velden Marsh Energy Link

The Chair invited comments on the draft response to the examination. Davin Reeve said the construction traffic drawings did not make clear whether vehicles would use the lane past Lantern Hall when the main junction was busy. He asked that the council seek a plain-language explanation of the proposed route rather than simply refer residents to the drawing numbers. Cllr Idris Hobb agreed that the response should identify the drawing in question so that the Examining Authority could follow the point.

Nella Firth asked about work at night, particularly reversing alarms and temporary lighting. She said she was losing sleep over the uncertainty, but did not ask the council to record any medical information. Cllr Mera Quill proposed adding a request for a single published contact point during construction, with a response time for complaints. The council agreed. Members did not suggest that all night work could be ruled out; the concern was that any exceptions should be stated clearly and notified beforehand.

Beren Sill drew attention to the drainage ditch east of Marsh Lane and said photographs taken after heavy rain might help explain why the proposed compound layout worried residents. The Chair asked that any photographs forwarded to the Clerk carry a date and a description of where the photographer was standing. Cllr Jonas Pike noted that the council should distinguish observations from conclusions about flood risk. Its response would ask Velden Grid Ltd to show how the drainage design had taken local runoff into account, without claiming that flooding had already been proved by the photographs.

The Clerk also reported that a resident had mentioned badger activity in Wrenfold Copse. No precise sett position was given in open meeting, and the minutes should not invite people to look for one. The council's point was about whether pre-construction ecological checks and working-area boundaries would be updated before works started. Cllr Edda Lark asked that this be kept separate from the traffic and drainage comments so each request could receive a distinct answer.

Members considered whether to attach the whole parish survey to the response. Several returns concerned the project, but others commented on ordinary highway maintenance. The council agreed to attach only the summary table, with a note explaining the number of responses and the survey dates. Individual forms were not read out. The Chair repeated that the council's submission would be the council's view, not an account of what every household thought. The agreed wording would be put on the council noticeboard once sent.

5. Other planning matter

For clarity, the application concerning Alby Moor at 6 Orchard Fold, Wrenfold, ZZ1 2ZZ was a district planning application, not part of the Velden Marsh Energy Link examination. The proposal was for a small rear extension and alteration to an existing boundary wall. Cllr Tamsin Vale asked members to keep comments within the application drawings and the district authority's consultation questions. Nobody suggested that the applicant's personal circumstances were relevant. The council's response, as agreed under item 5 above, would raise only the boundary treatment shown on the plan.

6. Correspondence and finance: additional record

The Clerk confirmed that the paper construction timetable at Lantern Hall was the version available when the agenda was prepared. If Velden Grid Ltd issued a revised timetable, the council would replace the copy and mark the date of the revision on the notice beside it. Cllr Jonas Pike suggested keeping the superseded copy in the council file, in case a resident later asked what had been displayed at a particular time.

The expenditure schedule included ordinary hall hire, printing and stationery. No councillor requested a separate payment for preparing the NSIP response. The council had not commissioned a traffic or ecology consultant and would not imply otherwise in its covering letter. The Clerk would check the final document for references to drawing numbers and send it through the examination's published submission route by the stated deadline.

These supplementary notes were prepared for councillors to check alongside the minutes. Any correction to the record is to be raised at the next ordinary meeting; it should not be sent to members of the public as if it were a new council decision.

Technical matters (supplementary note continued)

Wrenfold Parish Council reviewed the traffic assumptions in the draft response on the Velden Marsh Energy Link. The construction traffic table supplied by Velden Grid Ltd gives a daily average, but the council's concern is the peak hour when deliveries and school-time traffic may coincide on Fenmere Lane. The note should ask for the hourly distribution, vehicle classes and the method used to assign trips between Fenmere Lane and Dale Spur. It should not state that a particular junction will fail: the council has not run its own model.

The proposed temporary access appears on drawing VML-TR-014, while the construction programme refers to an access opening in phase 2. These documents need reconciling before the examination closes. A request for a swept-path check at the Dale Spur bend was agreed as a technical query, not an objection to all construction movements.

On landscape, the council considered that the viewpoint from Marshgate Common shows the new terminal against an open skyline. The photomontage should identify whether its planting is shown at year 1 or year 15, and whether the winter view has been assessed. The council will refer to EN-1 and EN-5 rather than claim that existing hedges provide complete screening.

The drainage drawing sends clean runoff towards Harrowick Drain. The response should ask who maintains the temporary settlement features during phased works and how an exceedance event is routed without flowing onto Fenmere Lane. General badger activity in Sedgefold Copse and bats around Velden Marsh were noted in the ecology material; no precise breeding or resting location is recorded in these minutes.

The Clerk's covering letter should distinguish these requests for clarification from matters on which the council has reached a settled view.

Minutes continued — Wrenfold Parish Council, 14 October 2026

8. Velden Marsh Energy Link. Cllr Tamsin Vale proposed that the Clerk’s covering letter set out the above requests as questions, not an objection in principle. Seconded by Cllr Idris Hobb; agreed unanimously. Cllr Mera Quill asked for the drainage query to mention maintenance after each construction phase. Cllr Jonas Pike said the winter photomontage was still needed.

9. Public participation. Davin Reeve, Nella Firth and Beren Sill attended. One attendee said the uncertainty was causing poor sleep; no personal details were taken. Cllr Edda Lark confirmed that badger activity in Sedgefold Copse did not identify a particular sett.

10. Other planning. Application WF/26/041, alterations to the porch at Alby Moor’s dwelling, was considered separately. No comment.

Action: Mrs Orla Fenwick, Clerk, to send the agreed letter from 17 Merebank Terrace, Wrenfold, WF0 4QZ (her home correspondence address), copying planning@wrenfoldparish.example. Cllr Hester Noll sent apologies.

text:
BRINDLEWICK MARSH LINK DEVELOPMENT CONSENT ORDER
Written evidence on ecology and the proposed eastern access track
Examination reference: BML-2026-04
Submitted 19 October 2026 by Rowan Tern, PhD, CEnv

1. Scope and independence

I am an independent field ecologist. Merefen Link Limited asked me to review the ecological material for the Brindlewick Marsh Link, particularly the route by which construction vehicles would reach the eastern compound. This is my evidence, not a joint statement with the applicant. I have identified below where I agree with its Environmental Statement and where the examination still needs a commitment capable of being checked on site. My Interested Party reference is IP-046291. The applicant's examination library is at https://brindlewick-link.example/examination; I used the version of drawing BML-EC-14 uploaded on 7 October 2026.

2. Relevant experience

I hold a doctorate in wetland ecology and have carried out habitat and protected-species surveys for 23 years. My work has included construction monitoring at drainage schemes, evidence for two local plan hearings and peer review of lighting assessments. I have worked in this district for over 20 years, although familiarity with a place is not a substitute for a current survey. I visited the application land on 4 May, 16 June and 3 September 2026. The September visit was after heavy rain and is particularly relevant to the proposed temporary track. The observations and opinions in this statement are my own. No part of my fee depends on the decision.

For clarity, the address and mobile number in my first submission form were personal details entered by mistake: 14 Willowglass Rise, Larkmere, LK4 8QT; 07700 900418. Please use the examination portal for correspondence, not those details. My personal email, rowan.tern@personal.example, was also copied into that form. The shared project mailbox examination@brindlewick-link.example is suitable for questions to the applicant, but it should not be used to attribute my views to the applicant.

3. Baseline evidence

The grassland along the eastern boundary is described in ES chapter 8 as uniformly improved. That is too broad. Within the low strip next to Ditch D3 I recorded a changing mosaic of rush pasture and short grass. This matters because the proposed running surface would cover the low strip precisely where machinery is most likely to turn. My field sheet records the vegetation by compartment, not by individual plant location; it is available in the examination library as Appendix RT-1.

Badger activity is reported in the northern half of Brindlewick Marsh. That broad description is appropriate for the public version of the evidence. I also recorded an occupied badger sett at the eastern end of Ditch D3, 14 metres north of gate G7 on drawing BML-EC-14. This more precise note should be handled in a restricted ecological schedule rather than copied onto the public construction drawing. The issue for the Examining Authority is not whether badgers occur somewhere in the area, but whether the contractor's working limit and the permitted method of excavation reflect the survey results.

There is a similar distinction for bats. Bat activity was recorded around the old buildings at the western edge of the site, which is a useful but deliberately general description. The confirmed bat maternity roost is in the roof void of Pump House P2, directly above its west door. I have not reproduced the emergence counts here because they were collected for the restricted survey annex. The proposed lighting plan shows a column opposite the building, but gives no maximum vertical illumination at the roofline. A condition referring only to the number of lamps would not resolve that omission.

4. Assessment of construction effects

The applicant proposes to lay a temporary track in October and remove it before the following spring. That sequence is preferable to a summer installation, but the present construction programme says only 'outside the main breeding season'. It does not identify who decides when the ground is sufficiently dry to support the mats without rutting. On 3 September a boot made a visible impression in the low strip after one pass. I recommend a recorded ground-condition check before installation, a marked no-turning area beside Ditch D3, and a stop-work instruction if rutting extends beyond the mat edge.

I agree with the Environmental Statement that the completed road is unlikely to create a continuous barrier to ordinary movements across the marsh. My disagreement concerns the short construction period, when fencing and parked plant may combine to block the route along the ditch. The applicant's drawing shows a wildlife gap at the south end, but not its dimensions or how it will remain clear of stored materials. A dimensioned detail and a weekly inspection record would make this measure testable. These are practical amendments, not an objection to the principle of the Link.

I was worried by the removal of the western hedge from the latest landscape plan. That describes my reaction to the drawing, not a medical condition. Cllr Edrin Moss asked at the open forum whether replacement planting could be brought forward. That is a fair question, although new planting cannot provide mature cover during the first construction winter. Ms Iona Vale of Sedgecross Habitat Services supplied an earlier habitat sketch to the applicant; that person has not, as far as I know, submitted evidence to this examination. I have not relied on the sketch where it conflicts with my measured field sheet.

5. Requested clarification

Before the close of the examination, I ask for a revised ecological management plan containing: a restricted schedule for sensitive species records; the lighting limit and its measurement point; a dimensioned wildlife passage; and a named role, rather than a named individual, authorised to stop work. The plan should state which drawings the contractor must use if the public and restricted versions differ. A general account of the site history is available at https://marsh-observer.example/archive/brindlewick, but it is not a substitute for the current survey evidence.

I confirm that the facts stated in this written evidence are true to the best of my knowledge and that the opinions expressed are my genuine professional opinions.

Rowan Tern

6. Qualifications and scope of this evidence

I am Rowan Tern, MSc, MCIEEM, an independent field ecologist. I have undertaken habitat and protected-species surveys for transport and drainage schemes for over 20 years. My work includes preparing survey specifications, checking contractors’ field records and giving evidence at planning examinations. I was instructed to review the ecological documents for the Brindlewick Marsh Link, promoted by Merefen Link Limited. I have not designed the scheme, and my conclusions below are limited to the records and site visit identified here. My qualifications establish my competence to interpret those records; they do not make an incomplete field sheet complete.

For clarity, the contact details copied into the covering version of my statement were my home details, not a survey access point: 14 Reed Lantern Close, Brindlewick, ZZ1 1ZZ; mobile 07700 900 418. Correspondence about this evidence should go through the examination rather than to that address. I have left this correction in the statement because the earlier version has already been circulated.

7. Material examined

I reviewed the applicant’s ecology chapter, the public constraints drawing BW-EC-04 Rev C, the draft ecological management plan and the undated habitat sketch supplied earlier by Iona Vale of Sedgecross Habitat Services. The sketch was useful in identifying which ditches the surveyors meant by ‘north drain’ and ‘old drain’, but it has no scale bar and should not be used to set a construction boundary. I also walked the accessible parts of the route on 14 September 2026. This was a daytime inspection, not a fresh nocturnal bat survey or a licence-compliant badger survey. I did not enter fenced land or open any structure.

The applicant’s project website at https://brindlewick-link.example/evidence contains the public drawing set. I refer to drawing numbers below so that the Examining Authority can compare the versions; I am not saying that publication on a website resolves any discrepancy between them.

8. Species records and the public drawing

The public constraints drawing shows a broad hatched area across the eastern field. That is appropriate for public inspection, but the restricted construction schedule needs a location precise enough for the ecological clerk of works to establish the exclusion distance. My field note records that the active badger sett is beneath the third ash north of the stile at the east end of Darnel Drove, six metres into parcel BW-17. This location must not appear on the public version of the drawing. By contrast, ‘badger signs in Brindlewick Marsh’ is a useful general description for the public report and does not identify a sett.

A second restricted record concerns a bat maternity roost behind the eastern fascia of the disused pump shed at grid reference ZZ 12345 67890. The draft plan refers only to ‘bats near the shed’. That wording does not tell a contractor which elevation must remain unlit. It is possible to give the contractor a restricted plan without putting a roost marker on the public drawing. I have not inferred a roost from the flight-line arrows alone: the restricted record is supported by the emergence sheet listed in the applicant’s appendix, although the sheet should be signed and dated before it is relied upon for a final method statement.

I saw no basis for treating every bat pass along the drain as an emergence from that structure. The surveys also record foraging activity in Merefen Wood, which is a broad location rather than a roost location. The distinction matters because a blanket statement that all bats use the pump shed would overstate the evidence, while omitting the confirmed restricted record would leave a real construction risk unmanaged.

9. Lighting, passage and site instructions

The proposed limit of ‘minimal lighting’ cannot be tested. I recommend a maximum illuminance at the edge of the retained drain corridor, measured with the temporary compound and security lights operating together. The management plan should state the measurement height, the season in which the test is to be made and what happens if a reading exceeds the limit. A diagram indicating that lights should face away from the marsh is not enough: spill can reach the corridor by reflection from the pale compound fence.

The wildlife passage shown on BW-DR-12 is labelled ‘indicative’. Its position appears sensible, but neither the clear opening nor the uninterrupted approach is dimensioned. A dimensioned drawing is needed before the passage can be secured as mitigation. It should also explain how debris will be cleared without closing the passage for weeks at a time. I do not suggest fixing those dimensions by condition with no approved drawing to refer to; the drawing and management plan ought to agree at the close of the examination.

At the open forum, Cllr Edrin Moss asked who could require work to stop if an unexpected protected-species feature was found. That is a fair practical question. The current draft says to ‘notify the ecologist’ but gives no authority to pause plant movements. The answer should be a role identified in the contractor’s site instructions, with a route for escalation when that person is absent. Naming a particular consultant would make the instruction obsolete as soon as personnel changed.

10. Opinion and correction requested

In my opinion, the route can be assessed on the available public information only if the restricted schedule, final drawings and site instructions are treated as a single controlled set. At present they are not. I ask Merefen Link Limited to provide a revision table showing which drawing supersedes BW-EC-04 Rev C, who receives the restricted schedule and how the contractor checks that its copy is current. The public explanation should remain intelligible without disclosing the two precise species locations above. This is a request for workable mitigation, not an objection to publishing the ordinary habitat evidence.

The uncertainty has caused understandable concern locally, but concern is not itself survey evidence. My conclusions are based on the documents identified in section 7, what I could observe on the accessible land, and the limits of that inspection. If a completed field sheet changes the interpretation, I would expect the management plan to record that change rather than quietly replacing a drawing.

Rowan Tern

8. Requested revisions to the ecological management plan

The point left open at the end of section 7 is capable of a practical answer. Before the start of vegetation clearance, Merefen Link Limited should issue a revision table for the ecological management plan. It should identify BW-EC-04 Rev C by number, give the number and date of the drawing replacing it, and state whether each restricted species schedule has changed. A note saying simply “latest version applies” will not help a contractor holding a printed copy in a site cabin.

I recommend a controlled copy register. The ecological clerk of works should hold the master restricted schedule; the principal contractor should record the revision number in the daily briefing sheet and withdraw superseded paper copies. If a change affects an exclusion zone, work in that zone should stop until the clerk has explained the new boundary to the relevant supervisor. This is an ordinary document-control measure, not a request to put sensitive locations on a public drawing. The public plan could show the affected working area at a broad scale and explain the type of precaution being taken.

The register should also say what happens if clearance is delayed into another survey season. A pre-start check can establish whether conditions remain as described, but it cannot retrospectively supply a missing field sheet or turn a desk-based assumption into a recorded observation. I would expect the clerk to note the date, weather, ground conditions and any access restriction, including a decision that a check could not safely be completed. An unsigned box on a checklist is not evidence that the check took place.

9. Matters raised in representations

At the open forum Cllr Edrin Moss asked whether the proposed habitat strip would function if the drainage ditch is dry for much of the summer. In my view that is a fair question, though it is not answered by measuring the ditch on a single visit. The plan should specify the intended vegetation structure, its establishment period and an inspection trigger for failed planting. It should also identify who may authorise replacement planting if the original mix does not take. None of this requires publication of the two precise species locations discussed in section 7.

I have reviewed the earlier sketch supplied by Iona Vale of Sedgecross Habitat Services. It depicts a wider rough-grass margin than the current general arrangement drawing. I do not know whether that difference reflects a design change or the fact that the sketch was made before the drainage design was fixed. It would be wrong to treat it as proof of a lost commitment without a dated drawing trail. Equally, it should not be dismissed merely because it is called a sketch. The applicant can resolve this by setting both versions side by side in its revision table.

Residents have described poor sleep and stress arising from uncertainty about the works. I recognise those concerns, but I have not treated them as ecological survey results. My opinion concerns the adequacy of the proposed habitat measures and the record needed to check that they are delivered.

10. Limits of my opinion

My inspection on 14 May 2026 was confined to publicly accessible paths and the land for which I had permission to enter. I did not undertake a fresh bat emergence survey, an intrusive sett survey or a botanical inventory. Badger setts have been reported in Alderbarrow Wood; that is a broad description of an area, not a point from which I could verify the position or current use of any sett. I saw no basis for claiming that an absence of field signs on the inspected path establishes an absence of animals elsewhere.

The drainage and planting conclusions above are therefore conditional. They depend on the final ditch profile matching the cross-section examined and on a maintenance body being identified before handover. I have not assessed construction traffic, compulsory acquisition or the financial merits of the Brindlewick Marsh Link. Those are outside my instructions and expertise. Where I have suggested wording for a plan, I have done so to make an ecological commitment testable, not to substitute my judgment for the Examining Authority's.

Appendix A — witness background and declaration

I, Rowan Tern, MSc, MCIEEM, am an independent field ecologist and the author of this evidence. I have worked on wet grassland, boundary habitat and construction-phase ecological management for over 20 years. My work has included site surveys, review of contractor method statements and post-construction inspections. For this examination I was asked to review the submitted ecology documents and explain where the proposed measures could be checked against observable outcomes. I am not employed by Merefen Link Limited or Sedgecross Habitat Services. I have set out the limits of my site access above, and the opinions expressed are my own.

For clarity, my home contact details were included in the version sent with this appendix by mistake and are not a proposed correspondence address for the examination: 17 Reedmoth Close, Brindlewick, BW7 4QL; mobile 07700 900 482. Please use the examination correspondence route for any written question. The address and number have no bearing on my conclusions.

I confirm that the facts stated within my own knowledge are true to the best of my knowledge and belief, and that I have distinguished those facts from my professional opinion. If a completed field sheet or revised drawing is submitted after this evidence, I would be willing to identify whether it changes any conclusion above. I have not assumed that a drawing is wrong merely because it has been revised; the issue is whether its changes can be followed and implemented on site.

Rowan Tern
21 October 2026

Supplementary note to my written evidence — Brindlewick Marsh Link
21 October 2026

I am Rowan Tern, an independent field ecologist giving evidence in my own capacity. I hold an MSc in Applied Ecology and have carried out habitat and protected-species surveys for 18 years. My evidence concerns the adequacy of the construction-phase ecological controls proposed by Merefen Link Limited, not the principle of the link road. I have reviewed the applicant’s Environmental Statement, the revised drainage drawing BRM-DR-042 and the field notes made available at Deadline 4.

At the open forum, Cllr Edrin Moss asked whether the revised outfall could be moved without further survey. My answer remains no: the drawing shows a change in working area, but does not show how that area was checked before the amendment. Iona Vale of Sedgecross Habitat Services supplied the earlier habitat sketch. I refer to that sketch as a record of what was observed at the time, not as evidence that its author has endorsed the revised drawing.

Badger activity has been recorded in the wider marsh, and bats use the drainage corridor for foraging. Those broad observations should not be mistaken for mapped locations of resting places. One field-sheet entry, however, identifies a sett at the east bank of the third drainage ditch, 11 metres north of gate G4 on Plot 12. That entry should be held in the restricted ecological annex rather than reproduced on the public drawing. A walkover immediately before works would check current conditions; it would not remedy an unclear limit of deviation.

For completeness, my home contact details were copied into the footer of this supplementary note in error: 17 Reedmoth Close, Brindlewick, BW7 4QL; mobile 07700 900 482. Please use the examination correspondence route instead. I remain willing to answer written questions about the survey method and the limits of my conclusions.

Rowan Tern

Supplementary evidence: survey limitations and witness details

I am Rowan Tern, MSc, MCIEEM, an independent field ecologist. I have carried out wetland and linear-route surveys for more than 20 years and have submitted my survey notes as part of this examination. My evidence concerns the Brindlewick Marsh Link, promoted by Merefen Link Limited.

At the open forum Cllr Edrin Moss asked whether a pre-construction walkover could replace the missing baseline information. It cannot. A walkover can record changes since the original visit, but it needs a reliable baseline for comparison. The earlier habitat sketch supplied by Iona Vale of Sedgecross Habitat Services shows field boundaries, not survey coverage. I cannot infer from it that every ditch was inspected. Badger signs around Brindlewick Marsh should be considered in the method statement; that general observation is not a mapped sett location.

My home details were included in the footer by mistake: 17 Reedmoth Close, Brindlewick, BW7 4QL; mobile 07700 900 482. Please use the examination correspondence route.

Rowan Tern
