Actions will have an owner and a close-out entry; a photograph alone will not count as evidence that a defect was corrected.

7.9.2 During operation, the landscape and ecological management plan (LEMP) will track establishment of replacement hedges and margins, the condition of ditch banks and the continued operation of the lighting controls. Fixed monitoring points will be used where access and vegetation growth permit, with the method and any departure recorded each year. Broad species observations, including bats near the western hedgerows and birds using the wider fields, may help interpret habitat use. They will not be presented as evidence of a breeding site or resting place without a suitable survey. Monitoring reports intended for general circulation will describe any sensitive finding at an appropriate scale.

7.9.3 The annual ecology summary will be supplied to Merevale District Council and Brindle Fen Drainage Board in accordance with the LEMP. It will identify completed management tasks, outstanding defects, changes to methods and any proposed corrective action. If a drainage inspection shows repeated sediment deposition despite compliant installation, the response will consider whether the control itself needs redesign, not merely whether another inspection is required. Conversely, a single low survey count in poor weather will not, by itself, establish a project effect. The comparison will use the agreed survey method and the context recorded for each visit.

7.9.4 Subject to those verification and reporting requirements, no change is made to the residual-effect conclusion in paragraph 7.8.10. The conclusion will be reconsidered if the final layout removes a retained habitat connection, increases permanent light spill or requires a ditch crossing outside the assessed envelope. Any such reconsideration will be documented before the relevant activity proceeds.

7.9.5 The annual ecology summary will distinguish between a measure being installed, a measure functioning as intended, and an ecological response being detectable. These are not interchangeable findings. Merevale Link Energy Ltd will provide the summary to Merevale District Council and Brindle Fen Drainage Board following each monitoring year. The underlying survey records will be retained so that an apparent change can be checked against weather, survey effort and changes in land management before a corrective action is selected.

7.10 Cumulative effects and conclusion

7.10.1 This section considers whether the Merevale Link Energy Project could act with other reasonably foreseeable development to affect the same ecological receptors. It draws on the assessment in this chapter and the project list in Appendix 7.6. The list was checked against the council's public planning register in September 2026. It is a snapshot for assessment purposes, not a prediction that every consented scheme will be built. Schemes with no plausible shared pathway, including works confined to existing buildings, were screened out with a reason recorded in Appendix 7.6.

7.10.2 The principal shared pathways are temporary disturbance during construction, interruption of habitat connections and changes to water quality in the drainage network. A construction programme overlap would not necessarily mean an ecological effect: the location of works, season, duration and intervening habitat all matter. Conversely, works carried out in different years could contribute to a longer-term reduction in habitat quality if restoration does not establish successfully. The assessment therefore considers both overlapping activity and the condition of habitat after construction.

7.10.3 The closest consented works comprise resurfacing on Fenharbour Road and improvements to the Brindle Fen drainage network. Resurfacing is largely within the existing highway boundary and has limited opportunity to combine with the Project's habitat loss. Short periods of concurrent vehicle movement could increase disturbance at the road edge, but the temporary works limits and retained boundary vegetation would separate that activity from the main habitat connections. The drainage improvements have a more direct potential pathway through suspended sediment. Their construction method is not yet fixed; the cumulative assessment has conservatively assumed that open-channel work could coincide with a Project ditch crossing.

7.10.4 Under that assumption, the Project's construction environmental management plan will require the crossing method, isolation arrangements and rainfall response procedure to be confirmed before work begins. The watercourse protection measures assessed in paragraph 7.7.18 apply irrespective of whether the drainage improvements proceed. They include keeping excavated material out of the channel corridor, providing suitable containment for pumped water and suspending in-channel work when controls cannot be maintained. The contractor will check the drainage programme at the pre-start meeting. This check is intended to coordinate practical controls; it does not transfer responsibility for the Project's own discharges to another scheme.

7.10.5 There is no evidence of a cumulative loss of a continuous corridor at landscape scale. The assessed layout retains the principal hedgerow connections and provides for reinstatement at temporary working gaps. The plans identify Larchmere Farm as a land parcel name, not as a separate ecological receptor. Habitat creation is shown at a scale that can be delivered within the Order limits, with establishment and replacement provisions in the landscape and ecology management plan. The assessment does not count proposed habitat as functioning on the day it is planted. Until it establishes, the retained vegetation remains the principal means of maintaining connectivity.

7.10.6 Survey results indicate use of the wider study area by bats and farmland birds, but the observations do not establish a single indispensable route or breeding site within the works area. References to bats along the southern field boundaries and birds in the fields near Larchmere Farm describe broad survey patterns, not the position of a roost or nest. The assessment relies on avoiding unnecessary night working, directing task lighting away from retained vegetation and checking vegetation before removal. These controls are specified by activity rather than by a fixed calendar date because weather and the actual construction sequence may change.

7.10.7 The lighting design has been assessed using the parameters in Figure 7.12, including column height, orientation and the maximum illuminated working area. Figure 7.12 is an assessment drawing; it does not permit lighting to be moved into retained habitat at detailed design. A revised arrangement would need to demonstrate that spill at the habitat edges remains within the assessed envelope. If it cannot, the ecological conclusion must be reviewed before the lighting is installed. Temporary security lighting will be switched off when it is not required for safe access or site protection, subject to the construction security assessment.

7.10.8 In-combination effects have also been considered alongside existing agricultural drainage and routine road use. Those activities form part of the baseline rather than additional schemes. The sensitivity of the ditch network means that a small, poorly controlled discharge could nevertheless be material locally. That is why the conclusion rests on defined prevention, inspection and response measures, rather than on an assumption that the receiving channels will dilute sediment. Monitoring will examine repeated events and the effectiveness of a control, as set out at 7.9.3, as well as individual exceedances.

7.10.9 On the available information, no significant adverse cumulative ecological effect is predicted once the embedded design and secured mitigation are applied. There is uncertainty about the timing of the drainage improvements and the rate at which new planting will establish. Neither uncertainty has been treated as evidence of benefit. The annual summary will record departures from the assumed construction sequence, failures of habitat establishment and the corrective work completed. Where a departure changes a pathway assessed in this chapter, Merevale Link Energy Ltd will review the conclusion before the relevant works continue. This is consistent with paragraph 7.9.4 and does not replace any separate consent or protected-species requirement that may apply at the time of construction.

7.11 Summary of residual ecological effects and monitoring

7.11.1 This section draws together the residual effects identified in Chapter 7 following the design measures described in Section 7.6 and the mitigation commitments in Section 7.9. It should be read with the Ecological Management Plan (EMP), which sets out the actions to be taken before, during and after construction of the Merevale Link Energy Project. The assessment concerns the land shown within the Order limits; it does not assume that habitats outside those limits will be available for mitigation.

7.11.2 The principal construction activities relevant to ecology are vegetation clearance, temporary access formation, trenching, drainage works and reinstatement. The working corridor has been narrowed beside retained hedgerows and the drainage channel. Temporary compounds are placed on existing hardstanding or regularly cultivated land where practicable. These design decisions reduce the area of permanent habitat loss but do not remove the risk of accidental damage at the working edge. Fencing, marked access points and a pre-start briefing will therefore be required before machinery enters each work area.

7.11.3 At Larchmere Farm, the land plans show a temporary working area adjoining an existing field access. The farm name identifies the mapped location only. The access will be widened for the construction period and restored when deliveries have finished. The adjacent hedge will be retained except for the short section identified in the vegetation removal schedule. Replacement planting will use locally appropriate native species and will be protected from routine verge cutting during establishment. The assessment assumes that the restored access margin will not be used for long-term storage.

7.11.4 The drainage design provides a continuous flow route beneath the crossing near B4627 Sedge Lane. Works in or beside the channel will be programmed for a period when disturbance to aquatic habitats can be minimised, subject to the drainage consent and conditions on the ground. Silt controls will be installed before excavation starts and inspected after heavy rain. Pumped water, if required, will pass through settlement measures rather than discharge directly into the channel. These are construction controls, not evidence that the channel will improve as a result of the scheme.

7.11.5 Surveys identified widespread bird nesting habitat in hedges and rough grassland. Clearance will ordinarily be undertaken outside the main nesting period. If this is not possible, vegetation will be checked shortly before removal and work will be deferred where an active nest could be affected. The survey record does not provide a basis for treating every hedge as occupied in every year. Equally, an absence of nesting activity on one visit will not remove the need for the pre-clearance check where the work is delayed.

7.11.6 Bat activity was recorded along several linear features, particularly where hedges connect with the wider landscape. The lighting design retains unlit routes along the principal field boundaries. Temporary lighting will be directed into the working area and switched off when it is not needed for safety or security. No conclusion in this chapter depends on a particular bat roost being present at a specified tree or building. If a feature with potential to support roosting bats must be disturbed, the applicable survey and licensing requirements will be reviewed before that activity begins.

7.11.7 Badger signs were recorded in the wider Brindle Wood area. This is a broad description of survey activity and does not identify a sett location. Construction staff will be instructed to report unexpected excavations or field signs to the ecological supervisor rather than investigate them with plant. Open trenches will be covered overnight or provided with an escape route where covering is impracticable. The same precaution will reduce the risk to other ground-moving animals.

7.11.8 During operation, routine vehicle movements are expected to be infrequent. Vegetation management presents the more persistent pathway for ecological effects. The EMP therefore specifies a varied cutting regime for grassland margins and limits cutting of newly planted hedgerows while they establish. It also requires invasive non-native plants discovered during maintenance to be recorded and controlled without spreading material along the corridor. These measures are intended to maintain the habitat assumed in the assessment, rather than to claim a measurable gain before it has occurred.

7.11.9 Monitoring will distinguish between completion of an action and its ecological outcome. A record that planting has taken place will not, by itself, demonstrate that a hedge has established. Checks in years 1, 3 and 5 will record survival, gaps, evidence of damage and whether replacement planting is needed. The annual ecology summary will also identify any drainage-control failures, unplanned vegetation removal or changes to the operational lighting arrangement. Photographs will be taken from repeatable viewpoints, but the summary will not publish precise locations of any newly identified sensitive wildlife features.

7.11.10 Fenharbour Ecology Partnership will prepare the monitoring findings for Merevale Link Energy Ltd. The annual summary will be provided to Merevale District Council and Brindle Fen Drainage Board in accordance with the proposed requirement. Where the monitoring identifies a failure, the summary will describe the remedial measure, the proposed date for completion and the check by which success will be assessed. A later report will confirm whether that measure was carried out; an outstanding action will not be recorded as complete merely because it has been scheduled.

7.11.11 With the embedded design and secured measures in place, the residual construction effects on ordinary field-margin and drainage habitats are assessed as not significant. That conclusion relies on the controls being implemented in the sequence described above. If the detailed programme brings drainage works and hedge removal into the same area at the same time, the combined disturbance will be reviewed before those works proceed. The operational assessment likewise relies on maintaining the retained habitat connections and controlling lighting. The remaining uncertainty is reported in the EMP monitoring programme and has not been converted into an assumed ecological benefit.

7.11.12 This section sets out how the conclusions in paragraph 7.11.11 will be checked during construction and the first five years of operation. It does not replace the requirements of the Outline Environmental Management Plan (EMP) or the detailed method statements prepared before each work stage. Rather, it identifies the observations needed to test whether retained habitats remain connected and whether the installed measures are functioning as assumed in the assessment.

7.11.13 The Merevale Link Energy Project comprises a cable connection, a converter compound and associated access works. For ecology purposes, the principal construction activities are topsoil stripping, temporary haul-road use, trench excavation and the installation of drainage crossings. The assessment distinguishes temporary occupation from permanent habitat loss. Temporary working areas will be reinstated to their former land use unless a drawing secured through the EMP shows a different habitat treatment. Reinstatement is not counted as completed simply when seed has been applied: the relevant measure is whether vegetation establishes and can be managed without repeated ground disturbance.

7.11.14 Merevale Link Energy Ltd will maintain a works register identifying the location, date and extent of each hedge opening, drain crossing and field-margin occupation. The register will be checked against the approved construction drawings before an area is released to the principal contractor. Where a change increases the width or duration of an opening, the ecological implications will be reviewed before the change is made. This includes changes presented as minor amendments to plant access; repeated small widenings could otherwise interrupt a continuous margin over a greater length than assessed.

7.11.15 The baseline surveys by Fenharbour Ecology Partnership recorded mixed arable margins, short sections of species-poor hedge and managed drainage channels across the order limits. Survey evidence indicates that bats use the wider Brindle Fen corridor for commuting and that badger field signs occur within the wider survey area. These are broad descriptions of habitat use, not records of a particular resting or breeding place. The drainage channels also provide seasonal foraging habitat for common amphibians and birds. Survey coverage and limitations are set out in Appendix 7C; absence of a record at a particular visit has not been treated as proof that animals cannot use suitable habitat later.

7.11.16 At Larchmere Farm, the land plans show a temporary working strip beside an existing field access. The farm name identifies the mapped holding only. The strip will be fenced to the approved width, and stored material will be kept out of the retained hedge margin. There is no proposal to light this working strip routinely. If task lighting is necessary for a short activity, it will be directed towards the work face and removed when the activity ends. Compliance will be checked during the site inspections specified in the EMP rather than inferred from the lighting specification alone.

7.11.17 Drain crossings are to be installed using the sequence on Drawing ML-EC-017: isolate the work area, maintain downstream flow, excavate the crossing, reinstate the bank profile and remove temporary controls only when the bank is stable. Sediment controls will remain available during reinstatement, including when the excavation itself has finished. A crossing inspection will record bank condition and any visible sediment release after the first substantial rainfall following completion. The inspection is intended to identify a need for repair; it does not imply that every rainfall event will be monitored.

7.11.18 The operational lighting design limits permanent fittings to the converter compound and access junction. The assessment assumes that the retained hedge connections are not illuminated continuously. A commissioning check will compare installed fittings, orientation and operating controls with the approved schedule. If a fitting is repositioned for maintenance or security, its effect on the adjacent habitat connection will be checked before it is returned to normal use. This requirement applies even where the replacement fitting has the same stated output as the original, because mounting angle and shielding also affect spill.

7.11.19 Establishment monitoring will take place in the first, third and fifth growing seasons after reinstatement. It will record vegetation cover, bare ground, invasive plant presence and the continuity of hedge planting. The purpose is to determine whether the specified habitat treatment has established, not to claim a gain from ordinary regrowth within a temporary work area. Failed planting will be replaced in the next suitable season. Where repeated failure occurs, the cause will be investigated before further planting is ordered; compaction, drainage and unsuitable cutting regimes may each require a different response.

7.11.20 Merevale District Council and Brindle Fen Drainage Board will receive an annual ecology summary for the construction period and for the monitoring years identified above. The summary will distinguish completed actions, actions in progress and actions not yet started. It will also identify departures from the approved measures and explain the corrective action and its proposed completion date. A photograph may demonstrate the condition of a margin at an inspection, but it will not, on its own, establish that a habitat has met the relevant establishment criterion.

7.11.21 This approach is consistent with Merevale Local Plan Policy NE4, which requires effects on habitat connectivity to be avoided or reduced through design before reliance is placed on compensation. It is also consistent with the mitigation hierarchy used in the Environmental Statement. The project does not rely on habitat creation elsewhere to justify an otherwise unmitigated interruption to the retained drainage and hedge network. The secured measures therefore remain necessary throughout construction, including phases when work is concentrated away from the converter compound.

7.11.22 On that basis, no additional significant residual ecological effect is predicted from the monitoring proposals themselves. Monitoring is a means of checking the assessment and triggering remedial work, not a substitute for the embedded design. If monitoring identifies a persistent break in a retained connection or a drainage bank that cannot be stabilised by the approved repair method, the matter will be reviewed through the EMP change procedure. The review will record the evidence, the proposed response and any need for further consultation before the revised measure is implemented.

7.12 Cumulative effects and in-combination assessment

7.12.1 This section considers whether the residual effects identified above could combine with other parts of the Merevale Link Energy Project or with reasonably foreseeable development. It does not assume that every recorded species uses every part of the Order limits. The assessment instead follows the habitat connections shown on Figure 7.6 and the construction sequence in the Outline Construction Environmental Management Plan (OCEMP).

7.12.2 The principal route by which effects could combine is temporary fragmentation of the drainage and hedge network. The cable corridor crosses several field boundaries before reaching the converter compound. Although individual crossings are short, simultaneous open excavations could interrupt more than one connection used by wildlife. The construction programme therefore requires crossings on the same connected route to be completed in sequence, unless the ecological clerk of works confirms that an equivalent passage remains available. Trenches will be covered or provided with escape ramps outside working hours. These are construction controls, not compensation for permanent habitat loss.

7.12.3 At Larchmere Farm, the land plans identify a temporary working strip beside existing agricultural access. The farm name is used here to identify the land parcel only. The assessment assumes that the strip will be reinstated to its previous profile and that no permanent lighting will be installed there. If the detailed design requires a wider strip, the change must be checked against the habitat-loss figures in Table 7.18 before works begin. It would not be appropriate to treat unused land elsewhere in the Order limits as an automatic offset.

7.12.4 The assessment has also considered the proposed Sedgeway Road junction works. Their footprint overlaps the construction access for the converter compound, but the two activities are treated as one disturbance source where they occur at the same time. Counting them separately would overstate the area affected. Conversely, the combined traffic and earthworks period is used when assessing dust deposition on retained hedges. Wheel washing, covered loads and a 10 m no-storage margin beside retained vegetation are included in the OCEMP.

7.12.5 Information supplied for the Merevale District Council development schedule identifies two other proposals within the wider study area: a consented storage yard on previously surfaced land and a proposed drainage improvement along Alderwick Drain. The yard has no identified loss of connected habitat. The drainage improvement has not yet reached a fixed design; the available outline indicates localised bank reprofiling rather than removal of the drain. For this assessment, overlapping construction periods have been assumed. That is a precautionary assumption and does not imply that either scheme is committed to the applicant's programme.

7.12.6 On that basis, a short-term increase in disturbance along Alderwick Drain cannot be excluded if both projects work there concurrently. The retained vegetated bank, directional lighting controls and staged reinstatement reduce the likelihood that the combined disturbance would result in a lasting break in the corridor. The residual cumulative effect is assessed as minor adverse during construction and negligible once planting has established. This conclusion depends on the reinstatement specification being implemented, rather than on a future survey finding no wildlife present.

7.12.7 Badger activity has been recorded in the wider Merevale East Wood area. This is a broad description of survey coverage, not the position of any sett. General records of bats along field boundaries have similarly informed the lighting design without being treated as evidence of a maternity roost. The cumulative assessment addresses these groups through habitat connectivity and disturbance controls. It does not publish or rely upon a precise protected-species location in this chapter.

7.13 Monitoring and adaptive management

7.13.1 Merevale Link Energy Ltd will maintain a single register of ecological commitments covering the cable corridor, converter compound and access works. Fenharbour Ecology Partnership prepared the assessment and the draft monitoring schedule. Responsibility for delivering the commitments remains with the applicant and, where a measure is passed to a construction contractor, will be set out in the relevant works package. The register will distinguish a completed action from an action whose ecological outcome has been demonstrated; installing planting is not, by itself, evidence that a hedge connection has recovered.

7.13.2 Inspections will take place following reinstatement and during the first, third and fifth growing seasons. The inspection form will record ground condition, plant survival, gaps in the hedge line, evidence of erosion and whether maintenance access has damaged a retained margin. Percent cover will be assessed using fixed-length sample sections so that results can be compared between visits. Photographs will be taken from repeatable viewpoints, but the monitoring report will describe any sensitive species records at an appropriate scale.

7.13.3 A hedge section will trigger remedial action if fewer than 80% of planted stems remain alive at the end of the second growing season or if a gap exceeding 5 m persists across a connection identified on Figure 7.6. Failed stems will be replaced in the next planting season with the approved native mix. Where losses result from waterlogging or repeated vehicle damage, replacement alone will not be considered an adequate response: the cause will first be investigated and the planting method or protection amended. Any change to drainage levels must be agreed through the EMP change procedure.

7.13.4 The drainage-bank checks will be coordinated with the Brindle Fen Drainage Board so that ecological repairs do not obstruct maintenance access or reduce conveyance. The annual ecology summary will be provided to the Board and Merevale District Council. It will identify outstanding actions, explain any departure from the approved thresholds and state when a further check is due. A missed inspection will be recorded as a missed inspection, rather than entered as a satisfactory result.

7.13.5 Operational lighting at the converter compound will be checked after installation and following any change of fitting. The check will confirm mounting angle, shielding and the absence of unnecessary spill onto retained boundaries. It will not use a single favourable reading as proof that the whole boundary meets the design objective. Where adjustment is needed, the fitting will be re-aimed or shielded before additional lighting is considered.

7.13.6 Subject to these controls, no significant adverse cumulative ecological effect is predicted. The conclusion will be revisited if the final construction sequence creates simultaneous closures of connected crossings, if a third-party drainage design materially changes the retained bank, or if monitoring shows that reinstatement is not establishing. Those are defined review circumstances, not a general ability to defer mitigation until after construction.

7.14 Otter and Schedule 1 bird appendix: survey findings and conservation measures

7.14.1 This appendix provides the confidential site-level interpretation behind the ecological assessment for the Merevale Link Energy Project. It should be read with the watercourse crossing drawings and the lighting controls described in section 7.13. The applicant, Merevale Link Energy Ltd, will supply the restricted-location schedule to the appointed ecological clerk of works before enabling works. Public copies should retain the conclusions and mitigation requirements below but omit the two pinpoint locations identified in paragraphs 7.14.4 and 7.14.7. Omitting those locations does not change the extent of the works shown on the application plans.

7.14.2 Fenharbour Ecology Partnership surveyed the drainage network in March, May and August 2026. Banks were viewed from accessible land and bridges; no entry was made into a possible holt. Tavi Rell of Fenharbour Ecology Partnership checked the field sheets against photographs after each visit. The project uses a local survey grid, prefixed ML, rather than an Ordnance Survey grid. A two-figure reference such as ML 42 27 denotes a broad survey square and is used here to explain the distribution of records. Decimal local-grid coordinates in the restricted schedule identify individual features and must not be copied onto public figures. Survey conditions were generally suitable, although high water in August obscured parts of the lower bank.

7.14.3 Otter evidence comprised footprints on two exposed shelves, a spraint on a bridge ledge and a well-worn route through vegetation. These signs establish use of the watercourse, not continuous occupation of every section. Records occurred across the broad ML 42 27 survey square and along the connected drain beside Larchmere Farm. The farm name identifies a land-plan feature; this appendix makes no finding about its occupier. No otter was observed during the visits. A photograph supplied by Ms Nola Venn showed an animal at the edge of a drain, but neither the date nor the camera direction could be verified, so it has been treated as supporting information only.

7.14.4 One feature was assessed as a probable holt on the basis of a sheltered entrance, fresh tracks and a dry internal shelf visible without disturbance. Its restricted record reads: under the south bank of the West Mere Drain, 6.4 m upstream of crossing C4, at local survey coordinates E 438.62, N 271.44 (H1). That description is sufficiently precise to permit the feature to be found and is not required for understanding the public assessment. A second recess farther along the same drain lacked corroborating signs and remains a potential resting place, not a confirmed holt. The distinction matters when setting out fencing: both features warrant care, but the evidence should not be overstated.

7.14.5 The crossing method avoids excavation of the retained bank at H1. Before vegetation clearance, the ecological clerk of works will inspect the accessible approaches without blocking entrances or placing cameras inside a feature. If fresh evidence indicates that the working area would disturb an occupied place, work at that location will stop while the method and any licensing requirement are reviewed with the relevant statutory body. Temporary fencing will mark a no-access area for plant and materials; its alignment will be issued to the contractor in a controlled drawing. Overnight trenches will be covered or provided with an escape ramp, and substances harmful to water quality will be stored away from the drain. The reinstated bank will be checked after the first high-flow event and repaired if erosion exposes the crossing works.

7.14.6 Bird surveys combined dawn watches with checks from established paths. A hobby was recorded hunting over the wider fen in May, and a pair gave repeated territorial calls later in the season. These observations alone would not establish a nest. Subsequent watches, conducted from a distance, recorded food delivery to one tree and repeated returns to the same point. No climbing or close photography was undertaken. Other raptor sightings over ML 42 27 were passage observations and have not been entered as breeding records. The location of trees with no confirmed breeding use is not withheld merely because a protected bird flew nearby.

7.14.7 The confirmed Schedule 1 nest is recorded in the restricted schedule as on the third mature alder east of culvert C4, 2.1 m above the downstream bank (nest S1). This is an exact nest location, unlike the broad survey-square references above. Construction access will be routed away from that bank during the breeding period, and the tree will be retained. The ecological clerk of works will set a precautionary exclusion area from observed bird behaviour and intervening screening, rather than treating a nominal radius as proof that disturbance cannot occur. The contractor will receive a marked working-limit plan but not a public map labelling the nest tree.

7.14.8 If works are proposed nearby in a later breeding season, a suitably experienced ornithologist will first establish whether the territory remains in use. A previous year's record is not, by itself, evidence of current occupation or abandonment. No vegetation clearance within the working-limit area will begin until that check is complete. If breeding behaviour is observed, the programme will be adjusted and the limit reviewed; moving a fence closer for convenience will not be an acceptable response. Monitoring will record observations and decisions without including pinpoint nest information in the public annual ecology summary.

7.14.9 Conservation measures will be reviewed at the end of each construction season. Fenharbour Ecology Partnership will provide Merevale District Council and Brindle Fen Drainage Board with an annual summary of crossing condition, bank reinstatement, otter field signs and compliance with bird working limits. A restricted annex may be supplied through an agreed secure route where a recipient needs exact locations for its functions. Public reporting will use reach names or coarse ML survey squares. The applicant will investigate any repeated loss of cover, blocked passage or unplanned lighting spill and record the corrective work. These measures are commitments for implementation and checking, not a prediction that wildlife will remain at fixed points throughout the project.

7.14.10 This appendix records the evidence used to set the otter and Schedule 1 bird working limits for the Merevale Link Energy Project. It should be read with the watercourse drawings and the construction environmental management plan. Merevale Link Energy Ltd will issue a controlled copy of the location schedule to those carrying out pre-start checks. The public version deliberately distinguishes between observations that can be shown by survey square and features whose exact position should not be circulated. An absence of signs on one visit has not been treated as evidence that a watercourse is unused.

7.14.11 The survey area comprised the open drains east of Larchmere Farm, the Merevale Cut and the connecting wet grassland. Fenharbour Ecology Partnership used a project grid marked ML; its first two digits identify a broad survey square, while the full ten-digit reference identifies a point within approximately one metre. The ML 43 square covers several reaches and is appropriate for public discussion of otter activity. ML 43820 66940 denotes the proposed crossing centreline at Crossing C-12, not an animal resting place. References in this appendix are survey coordinates rather than postal addresses or landownership identifiers.

7.14.12 Daylight walkovers were made in February, April and June 2026. Banks were inspected from existing access routes, without entering cavities or lifting cover. Spraints, footprints and a short slide were recorded beside the Merevale Cut in ML 43. These are evidence of use of the reach, but do not on their own identify a holt. A photograph supplied by Ms Nola Venn showed an otter on the towpath after rain; the image was not used to assign a resting-site location because its camera position could not be verified. Tavi Rell of Fenharbour Ecology Partnership checked the field sheets against the crossing drawings before the working limits were drafted.

7.14.13 One occupied resting feature was subsequently confirmed at ML 43826 67195, in the north bank of the east drain 6 m downstream of the stone headwall at C-12. Fresh bedding visible at the entrance and repeated tracks on the same approach were recorded on two visits. This description is retained in the controlled location schedule so that the exclusion fence can be placed correctly; it must not be copied to public site notices. A further possible cavity in the ML 44 square could not be inspected safely. It is treated as a precautionary survey trigger, not as a confirmed holt. General references elsewhere in the ES to otters using the Merevale Cut do not indicate the position of a resting site.

7.14.14 Works at C-12 will keep a continuous dry passage above ordinary water level while the temporary flume is in place. No lighting will face along the drain, and stored materials will remain outside the marked bank buffer. Before vegetation clearance, an appropriately licensed ecologist will check the bank from a safe position. If fresh occupation or a new resting feature is found, works affecting that bank will stop while the design and any licensing requirement are reviewed. The contractor must not assume that the point recorded in 2026 is the only place where an otter may rest during construction.

7.14.15 Schedule 1 bird checks covered the wet meadow margins, drainage-board maintenance strip and trees that may be affected by access widening. A singing bird heard within ML 44 in April was mapped to the survey square only; song did not establish a nest. The confirmed nest was at ML 44103 67482, in the third pollard west of the disused brick pump plinth, 4.2 m above ground on its canal-facing side. The tree is outside the permanent works but close enough to the temporary access for disturbance to be possible. The detailed nest entry and photograph remain in the controlled schedule. A general record of birds of prey above the eastern fields has not been assigned a precise point.

7.14.16 The access-widening method will retain that pollard. If work is proposed during the breeding season, a pre-start check will establish whether the nest or another nearby nest is active. The ecologist will set a disturbance limit appropriate to the species, behaviour observed and nature of the work; it will not be reduced merely because the temporary road has already been laid. Plant movements and noisy operations inside an active limit will be deferred unless a lawful, species-specific approach has been agreed. Contractors will receive a marked working-limit plan, rather than the nest photographs or full survey coordinates.

7.14.17 For comparison, the barn owl box at the Larchmere Farm implement shed is shown on the land plan and is not reported here as a Schedule 1 nest location. The broad notation “wet meadow, ML 44” likewise identifies habitat, not a nest. Field teams should not convert these coarse descriptions into pins in publicly shared mapping. Where a bird is seen carrying food, the observer should record the behaviour for the ecological supervisor without following it into cover simply to obtain a grid reference. Survey evidence may be sufficient to apply a precautionary working limit without locating every breeding attempt.

7.14.18 The conservation plan will be checked after each construction season against the commitments in paragraph 7.14.9. The annual public summary will report whether passage at C-12 remained open, whether bank vegetation recovered and whether bird working limits were observed. It may use reach names and ML survey squares, but not the controlled resting-site or nest entries. Merevale District Council and Brindle Fen Drainage Board may request the restricted schedule where precise information is necessary for their functions. Requests from the general site team should go through the shared mailbox ecology@merevalelink.example, so that only the working information required for a particular task is released. This arrangement does not replace the obligation to stop and seek ecological advice if circumstances on site change.

7.15 Residual effects and monitoring

7.15.1 This section draws together the ecology commitments for the Merevale Link Energy Project following the construction-season checks described above. The assessment assumes that the measures in the Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP), the Landscape and Ecology Management Plan (LEMP) and the controlled species schedule are secured and implemented. It does not assume that the absence of a record in a particular survey square means that a species is absent. Where vegetation clearance or earthworks are delayed beyond the survey validity period, the relevant pre-commencement checks will be repeated before work starts.

7.15.2 Merevale Link Energy Ltd will maintain a single register of ecological actions during construction. Each entry will identify the work package, the applicable plan requirement, the date of inspection and whether corrective action was required. The register will distinguish a completed action from an action that has merely been instructed. Fenharbour Ecology Partnership will review the ecology entries at the end of each construction season and identify any recurring issue, including repeated damage to temporary fencing or delays in establishing replacement planting. This review is intended to test whether the measures work in practice, not simply whether they appear on a drawing.

7.15.3 For watercourses, the principal construction risk remains the movement of sediment from exposed ground during heavy rain. The drainage drawings place settlement features upstream of the discharge points and provide isolation valves for incidents. Temporary controls will be inspected after significant rainfall and before dewatering begins. Material removed from a settlement feature must be stored away from the channel and not put back on the bank. Brindle Fen Drainage Board will receive the annual summary of inspections and any changes to the agreed maintenance approach. Routine maintenance must retain the designed flow capacity without stripping the whole bank in one operation.

7.15.4 The proposed crossing at C-12 has been assessed as a short, localised intervention rather than a permanent break in the watercourse corridor. Its effectiveness depends on keeping the margins free of stored materials and allowing planted banks to establish. Photographic monitoring will use fixed viewpoints on the public working drawings; it will not reproduce restricted species records. If the first growing-season inspection finds substantial bare ground, the affected area will be replanted in the next suitable season. The annual report will state the extent of remedial work, rather than describing an incomplete bank as recovered.

7.15.5 Hedgerow removal is limited to the lengths shown on plan ML-07. The LEMP provides replacement planting along the retained field pattern, with gaps at operational accesses only where required for safe visibility. New planting will use locally appropriate species and will be protected from construction traffic and grazing until established. The assessment treats replacement hedgerow as a developing habitat; it does not count a newly planted line as equivalent to a mature hedge in its first year. Establishment will be judged by survival, continuity and condition, with failed sections replaced in the following planting season.

7.15.6 Lighting during construction will be task-based and directed into the working area. No permanent lighting is proposed along the retained dark corridor near Alderwash Wood. Checks will record the position and direction of temporary lamps, because a compliant lamp specification alone does not prevent spill if the unit is turned towards a boundary. The ecology assessment refers to bats using the wider woodland edge but does not identify any maternity roost in this public chapter. Detailed records, where needed for a specific work instruction, remain in the controlled schedule referred to in paragraph 7.14.9.

7.15.7 Bird working limits will be applied to vegetation operations in accordance with the CEMP. A check immediately before work is required where the programme cannot avoid the breeding season; a check undertaken weeks earlier is not sufficient. The site team will record whether work proceeded, was adjusted or was postponed, without transferring restricted nest information into the general construction register. The assessment makes no claim that birds will cease to use the land around Larchmere Farm. It considers instead whether suitable habitat remains available during construction and whether replacement habitat is likely to establish.

7.15.8 Survey records indicate occasional otter activity along the wider Merevale Drain corridor. This is a corridor-level observation, not the location of a resting site. The crossing method retains passage at the channel margins, subject to the construction controls above. If field conditions differ from those assumed in the method statement, work at that location will pause while the method is reviewed. The presence of footprints or a path by itself will not be entered in the public register as evidence of a particular resting place.

7.15.9 Operational maintenance will principally comprise inspection of planting, drainage features and access tracks. Cutting will be phased so that not every managed margin is cut at once. The LEMP sets out the intended sequence but allows adjustments for weather and ground conditions; any adjustment must preserve the ecological purpose of the measure. Herbicide use is not assumed as the default response to poor establishment. Where a planting failure has resulted from compaction or prolonged waterlogging, the cause must be addressed before replacement plants are ordered.

7.15.10 Residual effects have been assessed after the embedded design measures and the secured mitigation, not after hypothetical future enhancements. Short-term disturbance to common habitats during construction remains, particularly where the temporary compound is reinstated. On the evidence available, no significant adverse residual effect is predicted for the assessed ecological receptors once the stated measures are in place. That conclusion is conditional on implementation and monitoring. It should not be read as permission to omit a control because a later survey has recorded fewer animals.

7.15.11 Merevale District Council and Brindle Fen Drainage Board will receive the annual ecology summary for the first five years of operation. The public version will describe progress against measurable commitments and explain departures from the programme in plain terms. It may include broad survey areas such as Alderwash Wood and the Merevale Drain corridor. Precise protected-site records will not be added to that version merely to demonstrate that a survey was undertaken. Requests for construction working information should continue to use ecology@merevalelink.example, so that the current approved drawing and instruction can be checked together.

7.16 Adaptive management and verification

7.16.1 The annual ecology summary described in paragraph 7.15.11 is an output of the monitoring programme, not a substitute for the underlying survey records. Fenharbour Ecology Partnership will retain the field sheets, photographs, habitat condition scores and inspection logs used to prepare it. The summary will distinguish between a measure completed as designed, a measure completed with an approved variation, and a measure still requiring action. Merevale Link Energy Ltd will maintain a separate register of corrective actions, with a target date and evidence of close-out for each item.

7.16.2 Monitoring will test whether the mitigation is functioning, rather than simply recording that it was installed. For example, the drainage-margin inspections will assess vegetation establishment, bank stability and the continued availability of an unlit passage along the Merevale Drain. Where a failed planting area leaves a substantial gap, replacement planting will be undertaken in the next suitable season. A short-term absence of recorded wildlife activity will not, by itself, be treated as evidence that the passage is unnecessary.

7.16.3 Habitat creation areas will be checked against the approved landscape and ecology drawings. The checks will record the area delivered, dominant vegetation, bare ground, evidence of waterlogging where relevant, and any encroachment by invasive plants. At Alderwash Wood, monitoring will concern the condition of the retained woodland edge and the adjacent buffer; it will not require public reporting of individual animal records. Survey methods will remain comparable between years, with departures from the agreed method explained in the technical record.

7.16.4 The first operational inspection will establish a practical baseline after construction. Subsequent visits will take place in seasons suitable for assessing the relevant feature, rather than on a single fixed calendar day. If a visit is delayed by flooding or unsafe ground conditions, the reason and revised date will be entered in the monitoring register. Comparisons between years will note differences in weather, access and survey effort so that an apparent change is not mistaken for a change in habitat condition.

7.16.5 Temporary construction controls will remain in place until the relevant permanent habitat or boundary treatment is effective. Removing temporary fencing, lighting screens or protective markers will require a recorded check against the approved drawings. Where construction phasing changes the order in which land is made available, the register will identify the interim arrangement and the date by which the permanent measure is expected. This is particularly important where works on one side of the Merevale Drain finish before works on the other.

7.16.6 The monitoring programme includes a response mechanism. If two successive inspections identify the same material failure, Merevale Link Energy Ltd will commission a review of the cause and propose a proportionate remedy. Possible remedies include additional planting, altered cutting frequency, repairs to a boundary treatment or changes to the timing of routine maintenance. The review will consider whether the original objective remains achievable and will identify any further permissions needed before works proceed. It will not retrospectively redefine a missed objective as having been met.

7.16.7 Construction and maintenance lighting will be assessed at the edge of retained habitat as well as within the working area. The relevant controls concern direction, shielding, duration and avoidance of unnecessary spill. A measured exceedance will be investigated alongside the actual equipment position and operating hours. The annual summary will report the nature of any recurring issue and the action taken, without publishing sensitive survey points. General references to bats using Alderwash Wood remain appropriate for the public summary; precise protected-site information is held in the restricted technical record.

7.16.8 Drainage maintenance will be planned so that ecological measures remain compatible with the operational requirements of Brindle Fen Drainage Board. Sediment removal and vegetation cutting may still be necessary to maintain conveyance. The method statement will identify the working width, access route and areas to be left undisturbed during each operation. This approach does not impose a blanket prohibition on maintenance: it requires the ecological purpose of the margin to be considered when the work is scheduled and carried out.

7.16.9 Where replacement habitat is delivered in more than one phase, monitoring will report each phase separately until establishment criteria have been met. Combining figures for newly planted and established areas could conceal a local failure. The annual table will therefore show the approved extent, extent delivered, extent meeting the applicable condition target, and any remedial work outstanding. Areas beside Larchmere Farm will be identified by the plot references used on the land plans, rather than by reference to any occupier.

7.16.10 Merevale District Council and Brindle Fen Drainage Board will be invited to comment on material changes to measures relevant to their functions. An amendment to maintenance frequency that affects an ordinary drainage channel, for instance, should be reviewed for both ecological and drainage consequences. Comments received and the resulting decision will be recorded. Routine adjustments within an approved method, such as changing a planting date because the ground is saturated, will still be logged but will not require the entire programme to be reopened.

7.16.11 At the end of year five, Merevale Link Energy Ltd will prepare a consolidated review of outcomes against the commitments in this chapter. The review will identify measures that can pass into ordinary site management and those that require continued targeted inspection. It will state the evidence for that conclusion, including unresolved defects and the proposed timescale for remedy. The end of the initial reporting period does not terminate a maintenance obligation specified elsewhere in the approved management documentation.

7.16.12 This framework is intended to keep the public account useful while retaining the detail needed for ecological verification. Broad location descriptions, such as the Merevale Drain corridor or Alderwash Wood, are sufficient for explaining progress. Detailed records can be considered through the appropriate controlled route where needed for implementation. The distinction protects the integrity of sensitive ecological information without preventing scrutiny of whether the promised measures were delivered.

7.16.13 The annual summary will report against measurable outcomes rather than treating completion of planting as evidence, by itself, of ecological success. Merevale Link Energy Ltd will provide the area of each habitat treatment, the proportion established and the action taken where a measure has not met its approved specification. Fenharbour Ecology Partnership will review the supporting survey records and distinguish a temporary seasonal variation from a defect requiring intervention. The summary will not publish coordinates for sensitive ecological records.

7.16.14 Monitoring will use fixed methods so that results from successive years can be compared. The baseline, construction-stage and operational-stage surveys will use the same broad habitat units, consistent recording seasons and stated weather constraints. Any necessary change in method will be explained in the report, with a note of the effect on comparability. A missing survey visit will be identified as a gap, not entered as a zero result. Photographs of habitat condition may be included where they do not reveal protected locations.

7.16.15 For grassland, the principal measures are sward structure, the extent of bare ground and the presence of the species groups specified in the approved seed mix. For hedgerows, the measures are continuity, survival and the establishment of a varied edge. The target is a functioning habitat mosaic, not a uniformly tidy verge. Cutting dates will therefore be adjusted where necessary to retain flowering and seed-setting plants, while maintaining visibility and operational access beside the internal track.

7.16.16 The Merevale Drain corridor will be managed as a connected feature throughout construction and operation. Temporary crossings will be limited to those shown in the construction plans and removed when no longer needed. The contractor will keep stored materials and refuelling activities out of the buffer identified in the approved drawings. Inspection records will note bank condition, shading and any sediment deposits associated with the works. These are practical checks on the effectiveness of mitigation; they are not a substitute for the separate water-quality controls.

7.16.17 Survey work has recorded bat activity along the Merevale Drain corridor. That broad description is sufficient for this chapter: it does not indicate a maternity roost or identify an individual tree. The proposed lighting design keeps permanent illumination away from the corridor, with task lighting during construction directed inward and switched off when the task ends. If a temporary work area cannot meet the approved lighting parameters, work will pause until a revised arrangement has been checked against the ecological method statement.

7.16.18 Badger signs have been recorded in Alderwash Wood, and the woodland will remain outside the permanent development footprint. This is a broad survey-area statement, not the location of a sett. The construction boundary will be marked before vegetation clearance, and site inspections will confirm that machinery, spoil and pedestrian shortcuts have not extended into the retained woodland. Routine inspections will record the condition of the boundary and any need to repair it, without reproducing detailed field records in the public annual summary.

7.16.19 Where vegetation removal is programmed, the ecological method statement will specify a pre-work check and a clear route for responding to unexpected findings. Checks are time-limited and do not replace the duty to avoid harm while work is under way. Nesting birds may use ordinary scrub and boundary vegetation in different years; accordingly, the programme allows for work to be deferred or the working area modified. No exact nest locations are required to explain that commitment in this chapter.

7.16.20 The restoration programme also addresses disturbed ground around the temporary compound near Larchmere Farm. The farm name is used as a land-plan reference and does not identify an occupier. Soil will be handled in the sequence specified by the soil management plan, with compaction relieved before seeding where testing shows it is required. The first inspection after reinstatement will distinguish failed germination from erosion, rutting or an inappropriate seed mix, since each calls for a different remedy.

7.17 Adaptive management and reporting

7.17.1 The proposed management schedule identifies trigger points for further action. If establishment falls below the approved threshold, the response may include gap planting, altered cutting, invasive-species control or a review of drainage conditions. A trigger is not, on its own, evidence that the overall mitigation has failed. It is a decision point requiring a recorded response and a subsequent check. Conversely, repeated failure against the same target will require a review of whether the original treatment remains suitable.

7.17.2 The first operational-year report is expected in 2027, subject to the actual commencement date. Subsequent reports will set out completed works, survey limitations, trigger events and outstanding remedial actions in a consistent table. Merevale District Council and Brindle Fen Drainage Board will receive the annual ecology summary for matters within their respective functions. Their receipt of the summary does not transfer the applicant’s maintenance obligations or imply approval of an unreported change to the management scheme.

7.17.3 Plot 14 is used in the application drawings as a land reference, not as an ecological record. Plan references will be retained in the controlled works documentation so that remedial instructions can be implemented accurately. In the public summary, broad features such as Alderwash Wood and the Merevale Drain corridor will normally provide sufficient context. Where a proposed remedial action could affect a protected feature, its detailed location will be supplied through the controlled route described at paragraph 7.16.12.

7.17.4 This approach is consistent with Merevale Local Plan Policy E7, which seeks measurable enhancement and long-term management of retained habitats. It also keeps the chapter proportionate: the assessment explains what will be protected, how effectiveness will be tested and what happens when a target is missed. Final prescriptions remain in the approved management documentation. Nothing in this reporting arrangement permits a reduction in the mitigation shown on the certified plans without the appropriate approval.

7.17.5 The monitoring programme will be delivered in three stages: pre-construction verification, checks during construction and post-construction habitat monitoring. Its purpose is to test whether the measures assessed in this chapter are functioning, rather than to repeat the full baseline survey every year. The programme will be secured through the Landscape and Ecology Management Plan (LEMP) and the Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP). Merevale Link Energy Ltd will remain responsible for ensuring that the requirements are carried through into contractor method statements.

7.17.6 Before works begin in each construction area, the limits of working, retained vegetation and relevant exclusion fencing will be checked against the certified plans. The check will also record any material change in habitat condition since the baseline surveys. If a change affects the assumptions used in the assessment, works in the affected area will not start until the necessary review and any revised method have been agreed under the relevant approval process. A routine seasonal change, such as a grassland being cut or a ditch temporarily holding less water, will not of itself trigger a revised assessment.

7.17.7 During construction, inspections will concentrate on the measures most likely to be disturbed by plant movements: fencing at retained habitat edges, temporary drainage controls, the condition of soil stores and the reinstatement of working strips. The ecological clerk of works will keep an inspection log identifying the area checked, the measure observed, any action requested and whether that action has been completed. The log will be available to Merevale District Council on request. It is not intended that every inspection note should be submitted as a separate examination or discharge document.

7.17.8 The Merevale Drain corridor will remain outside the permanent operational footprint, apart from the crossings shown on the certified plans. At each crossing, the construction method will maintain the continuity of the watercourse and avoid unnecessary lighting of the banks. Temporary sediment controls will be inspected after heavy rainfall while exposed ground is present. Where turbid runoff is observed leaving a work area, the immediate response will be to stop that pathway, check the control and repair or replace it before the activity resumes. This is an operational trigger; it does not depend on waiting for an annual monitoring report.

7.17.9 Reinstated grassland will be assessed by reference to establishment, cover and the presence of undesirable species, rather than a single fixed count of plants. The LEMP will set out the sampling approach and the thresholds appropriate to each seed mix. A failure to meet a threshold in the first growing season will normally lead to a review of ground conditions and management before reseeding is proposed. For example, a dense crop of annual weeds may require cutting and removal, whereas persistent bare ground may point to compaction or unsuitable topsoil handling. The choice of remedy will be recorded, with a date for checking whether it worked.

7.17.10 Hedgerow replacement will be checked for survival and continuity at the end of each growing season during the establishment period. Gaps arising from plant losses will be filled in the next suitable planting season using the species specified in the LEMP. The assessment assumes that replacement planting will develop as a connected feature over time; it does not assume that newly planted stems provide the same cover as an established hedge immediately. Temporary construction effects and the time taken for planting to mature have therefore been considered separately in the effects assessment.

7.17.11 Alderwash Wood has been treated as a broad survey area and as a retained habitat in the assessment. General references to bats, badgers and nesting birds within that area do not identify an individual roost, sett or nest. The public monitoring summary will likewise describe trends and management actions at habitat level. Should a future survey identify a feature for which precise location information requires restricted handling, the controlled reporting route described in paragraph 7.16.12 will be used. This distinction allows the effectiveness of mitigation to be scrutinised without publishing a location that could increase disturbance.

7.17.12 Lighting checks will be undertaken after installation and following any material change to the operational lighting arrangement. The checks will compare the installed fittings, direction of light and hours of operation with the approved lighting strategy. If spill onto a retained habitat exceeds the approved design parameters, adjustments such as shielding or re-aiming will be made and the affected area checked again. The strategy does not rely on an assumption that all operational areas will be unlit; it relies on light being confined to where it is needed for safe operation.

7.17.13 An annual ecology summary will bring together the results of habitat establishment checks, relevant construction inspection findings and outstanding remedial actions. It will be provided to Merevale District Council and Brindle Fen Drainage Board for information. The summary will distinguish a target that has not yet been achieved from a measure that has failed and will explain the proposed response in either case. Where an action is carried forward, the following summary will report its outcome rather than simply repeating the original recommendation.

7.17.14 The conclusions in Chapter 7 remain subject to implementation of the secured mitigation and management measures. With those measures in place, no significant residual adverse effect on the retained habitat network is predicted. The monitoring framework provides a means of testing that conclusion during delivery and operation; it is not a substitute for the measures themselves. Any proposal to depart materially from the certified plans or approved management documents would need to follow the applicable consent procedure and be assessed on its own merits.

APPENDIX 7.O — OTTER AND SCHEDULE 1 BIRD CONFIDENTIAL SURVEY NOTE
Merevale Link Energy Project | Environmental Statement | October 2026

7.O.1 This appendix supports the conclusions in Chapter 7 and the monitoring framework described at paragraph 7.17.14. It records the evidence for otter use of Merevale Drain and for breeding birds requiring particular care. Locations capable of directing a person to a holt or active nest are included here for assessment purposes; the public-facing ecology summary uses less precise descriptions. Nothing in this note changes the mitigation secured through the Outline Ecological Management Plan.

7.O.2 Fenharbour Ecology Partnership walked accessible banks and field margins in February, April and June 2026. Surveyors checked suitable roots, cavities, undercut banks and crossing points without entering them. Bird watches were undertaken from existing paths, with binoculars, so that nest approaches were not created. Field notebook entries were made by Tavi Rell, an employee of Fenharbour Ecology Partnership. Photographs were numbered in the project archive rather than appended to the public copy. Surveys are a snapshot: water levels after heavy rain made some bank sections impossible to inspect in April, and an absence of signs there must not be read as absence of otters.

7.O.3 For orientation, the relevant reach of Merevale Drain is shown at the coarse reference TL 47 73. Alderwash Wood, approximately 1 km north-east of the proposed cable corridor, was also checked for commuting and feeding activity. These references identify broad survey areas, not resting places. The Larchmere Farm name appears on the land plans solely to identify the adjoining field block; no inference about occupation of the farm has been made.

7.O.4 Otter spraints of different apparent ages were recorded at two drain crossings. A short slide and footprints on a muddy shelf were recorded after the June visit. The evidence supports regular passage along the drain, although it does not establish the number of animals using it. A photograph supplied by Ms Nola Venn shows what appears to be an otter on the watercourse in winter. Its date and position could not be independently verified, so it has been treated as supporting context only, not as proof of a breeding site.

7.O.5 One occupied resting feature was identified: the otter holt beneath the exposed roots on the south bank of Merevale Drain, 18 m downstream of the eastern Larchmere Farm field-gate crossing (TL 48216 73642). Fresh spraint and repeated tracks led into the opening. Surveyors did not test the cavity or install a camera there. The feature has been treated as a holt on a precautionary basis, whether or not young were present during the visits. Elsewhere, possible resting habitat occurs intermittently along the drain, but no second holt was confirmed. The distinction matters for setting out: a general description of suitable banks must not be used in place of the recorded constraint point.

7.O.6 Bird survey effort covered reed margins, the wet grassland mosaic and Alderwash Wood. At the broad scale, a marsh harrier territory was associated with the wetland in TL 47 73. Its nest was located on the low reed island immediately west of the drain's fork below the southern maintenance bridge (TL 47984 73461). Adults carrying food were watched from the path on two dates; the island was not visited. A hobby was also seen hunting over Alderwash Wood. Its active nest was identified in the upper fork of the lone pine beside the wood's eastern ride, 12 m north of ride marker AW-6 (TL 48672 74109). The latter observation was made from outside the wood boundary. Other bird records, including reed warbler song and an old, unoccupied corvid nest, are retained in the routine survey schedule and do not indicate further Schedule 1 nesting locations.

7.O.7 The working drawings show the drain crossing by trenchless installation and retain the wetland and woodland edges. They do not authorise vegetation clearance wherever a line on a plan looks clear. Before works near the drain, the ecological clerk of works will verify that the recorded holt remains outside the disturbance area and will check for newly established resting places. If its status or the construction method changes, work in the affected area will pause while the necessary legal advice and any licence requirements are resolved. No lighting will be directed at the drain during night working, and temporary fencing will keep plant out of the retained bank vegetation.

7.O.8 The breeding-bird controls are seasonal as well as spatial. Vegetation removal in the wetland and at the woodland edge is programmed outside the breeding period where practicable. Where that is not possible, a suitably experienced ecologist will check the affected area immediately before work; a negative check is valid only for the area and time inspected. If an active nest or territorial behaviour is found, the clerk of works will establish a disturbance-free area appropriate to the species and the activity, and work will not resume until advised that it can do so lawfully. The precise nest positions above are not to be copied onto general site noticeboards or distributed with the public method statement.

7.O.9 Habitat management will retain a continuous vegetated corridor beside Merevale Drain, with invasive-plant control undertaken from established access points. Reed cutting, where needed to maintain habitat diversity, will be rotational and informed by the preceding season's bird records. Monitoring will record otter field signs, the condition of retained banks and evidence of breeding-bird use; it will not rely on repeated approaches to a known nest. An annual summary will be provided to Merevale District Council and Brindle Fen Drainage Board. That summary may report broad areas and outcomes, but the restricted location schedule will be supplied separately where needed for a defined management or regulatory purpose.

7.O.10 The measures above form part of the wider ecological mitigation strategy for the Merevale Link Energy Project. This section explains how the measures will be secured during construction and how their effectiveness will be checked once the works are complete. It should be read with the Outline Landscape and Ecological Management Plan (OLEMP) and the Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP). The OLEMP sets the intended management outcomes; the CEMP addresses working methods, responsibilities and hold points during construction. Neither document removes the need to respond to conditions found on site.

7.O.11 The working area has been designed to avoid direct loss of Alderwash Wood and to retain the principal vegetation beside Merevale Drain. Temporary access across existing arable land will be reinstated following installation. Hedgerow gaps required for plant movements will be kept to the widths shown on the construction drawings and replanted in the first suitable planting season. Where a gap cannot be closed immediately, temporary screening will be considered where practicable; it must not obstruct drainage maintenance or create an unsafe working area.

7.O.12 Before each construction phase begins, the relevant working limits will be marked on the ground. The ecological briefing will cover retained vegetation, open excavations, artificial lighting, pollution prevention and the procedure for stopping work if an unexpected ecological constraint is encountered. A check immediately before vegetation clearance will establish whether the proposed method remains appropriate. The absence of a record in the baseline survey is not, by itself, permission to proceed without that check.

7.O.13 Seasonal timing will be used as a first means of avoiding impacts on breeding birds. If vegetation removal is needed during the breeding season, a suitably competent ecologist will inspect the affected area before removal. An active nest, if found, will be protected until it is no longer in use. The protection distance will depend on the species, activity and nature of the works, rather than a single fixed buffer applied throughout the site. The public construction drawings will show the general areas subject to this procedure, not the positions of any sensitive nests.

7.O.14 Surveys recorded general badger activity in the wider landscape, including signs within Alderwash Wood, but this chapter does not publish sett positions. No conclusion about occupation should be drawn from the age of a path or an isolated print. Pre-construction checks will inform the final access arrangement and any necessary licensing decision. Similarly, bat activity along the drain and hedgerows is treated as evidence that these features have a corridor function; it is not presented as proof of a maternity roost. Existing trees to be retained will be protected in accordance with the approved construction drawings.

7.O.15 Lighting during construction will be limited to what is needed for safe work. Where lighting is necessary near retained habitat, fittings will be directed into the working area, with the lowest practicable mounting height and duration. The final lighting schedule will identify temporary tasks and any operational security lighting separately. Floodlighting the full corridor as a standard site-security measure is not proposed. Merevale Link Energy Ltd will review any request for additional lighting against the ecological commitments before it is installed.

7.O.16 The drainage design provides for the separation of clean runoff from areas where fuel, concrete or disturbed soil could enter surface water. Stockpiles will be set back from the watercourse and covered or stabilised when required by conditions. Plant refuelling will take place in designated areas, with spill materials available at the point of use. These are construction controls, not a claim that the receiving environment has no sensitivity. The CEMP will specify inspection after heavy rainfall and the action to take if a control fails.

7.O.17 Habitat reinstatement will use a locally appropriate seed mix and planting suited to the soils and maintenance requirements. The objective is a varied structure, including rough grassland and scrub margins, rather than uniform short grass across all temporary working land. At Larchmere Farm, the land plans distinguish the temporary working area from permanent infrastructure; the farm name identifies a mapped site and does not indicate who occupies it. Management prescriptions will apply only to land within the agreed project controls.

7.O.18 Monitoring will test outcomes, not simply confirm that planting took place. Fenharbour Ecology Partnership will prepare a baseline condition record before the main works, followed by checks in the first, third and fifth growing seasons after reinstatement. The checks will consider establishment, invasive plants, gaps in the drain-side corridor and any persistent bare ground. If a prescribed outcome is not being met, the annual review will identify a corrective measure and the next date for checking it. Results will be presented at a scale useful for assessing habitat condition without disclosing protected-site locations.

7.O.19 The annual ecology summary described in paragraph 7.O.9 will distinguish completed actions from actions deferred because of weather, access or ecological constraints. Merevale District Council and Brindle Fen Drainage Board will receive the same account of the measures relevant to their functions. Any restricted location schedule will be handled separately from the public summary. A reference to badger signs in Alderwash Wood, for example, is sufficient for the public account; a precise field location is not needed to explain the overall management outcome.
